# Issue #1154: One Shell-Argument Reading for the Whole Agentic Module

Issue [#1154](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1154) (E119):
Codex's shell tool `exec_command` sends the command under the argument key
`cmd`, while `progress.rs` read only `command`. The work-item read was never
recorded as attempted, and the stateless planner re-derived the identical
`gh issue view` call 78 times in a row (6.2M input tokens) until the client
compacted the thread. The full incident account, with the transcript excerpts,
is `docs/case-studies/issue-1154/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1154-1 | One shared `command_argument` for the whole `agentic_coding` module, reading the argument key from the client's declared tool schema (the key whose schema describes the shell command), falling back to `command`, `cmd`, `script`, and an array form joined for `shell`-style tools; the seven local copies are deleted. | Implemented: `rust/src/agentic_coding/tool_result.rs` gains the shared `command_argument` (string and joined-array forms) and `command_argument_key` (schema-driven key resolution for callers that hold the request's tool definitions); the seven former copies in `progress.rs`, `file_read.rs`, `tool_result.rs`, `narration.rs`, `command_reroute.rs`, `evidence_record.rs` and `workspace_change.rs` now delegate to it. |
| R1154-2 | Invariant independent of parsing: never plan a tool call whose name and arguments are byte-identical to one already attempted in the current turn window; if the planner would, report the stuck step and its last result instead of repeating it. | Implemented: `Progress::repeated_call` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/progress.rs`) recognizes a completed call by byte-identical arguments or the same canonical command/URL operand (the protocol layer may project `command` onto `cmd` before the transcript echoes the call), and `stop_repeated_call` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/planner.rs`) replaces the repeat with the `stuck_step_report` answer from `data/meta/work-item-steps.lino`. A completed call is the loop signature; a failed one keeps its existing bounded retry and the two-failure stop of issue #1133. |
| R1154-3 | After a successful read, the fetched text drives `plan_work_item_execution` exactly as on the Claude and Agent paths. | Implemented by the shared reading: `issue_view_url` now resolves under `cmd`, the read lands in `fetched_pages`, and `repository_work_item_objective` feeds `plan_work_item_execution` unchanged. Pinned by `codex_cmd_read_drives_execution_instead_of_repeating`. |
| R1154-4 | Tests: replay the Codex transcript's first two Responses items (`function_call` `exec_command {"cmd": …}` + `function_call_output`) through the Responses input conversion and assert the next plan is not another `gh issue view`; a table test over `{command}`, `{cmd}`, `{script}`, `{command:[…]}` yields the same recorded read. | Implemented in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1154_progress_arguments.rs`: the replay goes through `ResponsesRequest::to_chat_completion_request` (the server's own conversion), and the table covers all four spellings plus the twice-repeated transcript shape. |

# Issue #1155: Work-Item Read Validation and Honest Fallbacks

Issue [#1155](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1155) (E120):
an unauthenticated `gh issue view` printed its how-to-authenticate banner, the
Agent CLI echoed that output with the exit status dropped (`"metadata":
{"exit": 4}` in its own record, plain text in the tool message Formal AI
received), and the banner was accepted as the issue body. The run then wrote
`.formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino` and answered `planned_not_executed`
without ever trying the `webfetch` tool the client offered. The full account,
with the transcript excerpts, is `docs/case-studies/issue-1155/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1155-1 | The read observes its own status whatever the client sends: the planned read ends with `printf '\n__formal_ai_exit=%s\n' $?`, as data in `data/meta/work-item-steps.lino` (`issue_view_command`), and a non-zero status is a failed read. | Implemented: `issue_view_command` in `data/meta/work-item-steps.lino` (and the byte-identical embedded mirror) now appends the sentinel `printf`; `exit_sentinel` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/progress.rs`) reads the last `__formal_ai_exit=N` line and `work_item_read_failure_reason` turns any non-zero status into a failed read even when the client's echo carries no error flag. |
| R1155-2 | The read's shape is validated before it is accepted as the issue: a title line, a blank separator, then the body — output without that shape is a failed read, recorded with its text. | Implemented: `work_item_read_failure_reason` requires the `gh` reads to contain the blank-line separator (the incident banner has none) and the raw-body `curl` read to be non-empty text that does not begin like the API's JSON error blob; failed reads land in `Progress::failed_work_item_reads` with their reason and are never pushed to `fetched_pages`. Pinned by `a_status_less_gh_banner_is_a_failed_read_and_webfetch_of_the_issue_follows` and `a_failing_sentinel_outranks_a_well_shaped_output`. |
| R1155-3 | On a failed read, walk the fallbacks in order and record each attempt: the client's fetch tool on the issue URL, `curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/<issues|pulls>/<n>`, `gh api`, then the prepared PR's title and body. | Implemented: `plan_work_item_read` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/general_execution.rs`) now plans, after the failed `gh` view: the fetch tool on the issue URL, `issue_rest_read_command` (credential-free `curl` with the raw-body `Accept` header), `issue_api_read_command` (two `gh api` calls printing title and body), and last `prepared_pull_reference` — the pull request the prompt names, fetched as page context. Pull-request work items read their REST `pulls/` endpoint. Every attempt is recorded; `Progress::work_item_read_attempts` lists them. Pinned by `the_rest_routes_follow_the_fetch_fallback_in_order`, `the_rest_fallback_of_a_pull_request_reads_the_pulls_endpoint`, `the_prepared_pull_request_is_the_last_read_fallback`. |
| R1155-4 | Only when all routes fail is `planned_not_executed` honest: the answer lists every read tried with its result, and the only write is never spent on the plan record when the goal could not be read. | Implemented: `work_item_read_failure_report` (filled from the `read_failed_report` data key) closes the run with every read, its reason and its first answer line — and `general_change_step` returns it before the `PLAN_PATH` write, so no plan record is written for an issue the session never read. Pinned by `an_exhausted_retrieval_reports_every_read_and_writes_no_plan_record`. |
| R1155-5 | Replay test from the transcript: with the Agent tool list (`webfetch`) and the `gh` result without exit status, the next plan is the `webfetch` of the issue URL; with the sentinel line `__formal_ai_exit=4` the read is a failure. | Implemented in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1155_read_validation.rs` (the file name the dispatch directed; the issue's Definition of Done names `issue_1155_work_item_read_failure.rs` — same tests, rename at registration if preferred): `a_status_less_gh_banner_is_a_failed_read_and_webfetch_of_the_issue_follows` replays the status-less echo, `with_the_sentinel_line_the_read_is_a_failure_and_the_fetch_follows` replays it with `__formal_ai_exit=4`, and both assert the next plan is the `webfetch` of the issue URL. |

Residuals for the main session: `REQUIREMENTS.md` and
`docs/requirements-traceability.md` regeneration
(`rust-script scripts/assemble-requirements.rs --write`), test registration in
`rust/tests/unit/mod.rs`, and the released-version manual confirmation row of
the issue's Definition of Done. Both ledger copies of
`data/meta/work-item-steps.lino` were edited byte-identically (the data/meta
tree is nominally main's; the issue requires the sentinel and the fallback
wording to live there as data).

## Issue #1156: Single output obligations

Source: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1156

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Preserve the requested behavior in the agentic harness | Repeated identical quoted stdout requirements are deduplicated in first-mention order; distinct output operands retain their order. The generated output verifier therefore compares against the composed single obligation. Workflows use the recipe artifact stem rather than a shared run.yml path. | Drafted. Inline regressions cover duplicate and distinct output requirements. Existing output-verifier template already uses byte comparison and propagates process failure. No local execution was performed. Repository/task-specific workflow naming beyond artifact stems remains open. |

## Issue #1157: Idempotent recipe commits

Source: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1157

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Preserve the requested behavior in the agentic harness | Recipe commits stage only declared artifacts and inspect the cached diff restricted to those paths. No-change runs emit __formal_ai_commit_unchanged, then still push and print the current hash. Continuations consume the planner evidence window, retaining already completed writes and commands. | Partial. Idempotent commit and continuation replay are drafted. Output ignore patterns and verification of artifacts after externally modified continuation state remain open. No local builds or tests were run. |

## Issue #1158: Pull request completion and feedback

Source: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1158

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Preserve the requested behavior in the agentic harness | After a verified recipe commit, PR targets retrieve comments and reviews, update their description from artifact and verification commands, and mark draft PRs ready only with a clean working tree. Already-ready PRs are accepted. Nonempty comments, requested changes, or unreadable feedback block readiness with the observed feedback. | Partial. Feedback retrieval, description editing and guarded readiness are drafted. Deriving and applying arbitrary review-requested source edits remains open; feedback is never represented as resolved merely because it was fetched. |

## Issue #1159: Workspace prerequisite recovery

Source: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1159

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Preserve the requested behavior in the agentic harness | Run failures are classified with the shared prerequisite classifier. Missing executables with FORMAL_AI_INSTALL_GRANT=workspace fetch their pinned publisher. A public process-free parser accepts only typed setup notation with a postcondition. Harness tools execute scoped setup, postcondition and one original-command retry, with explicit PATH and transcript binding; absolute/parent write scopes and shell/escalation setup programs are refused. | Partial. Typed publisher recovery is drafted and bounded. Ordinary publisher prose cannot become an executable recipe. Broader source discovery, per-process/network grants and typed recipes for publisher pages that lack them remain open. No local process installation, build or test was executed. |

## Issue #1160: Hive Mind prepared work continuation

Source: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1160

| Requirement | Drafted behavior | Status |

## Issue #1161 Client Registry Names the Agent Config Env

Issue [#1161](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1161) (E126)
makes the client registry declare *how* a client is pointed at its config —
the env var that relocates it — instead of implying an `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`
relocation that also moves `gh`'s and git's config and breaks GitHub
authentication inside the session. The incident analysis, the per-client
evidence, and the fix live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1161/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1161-1 | Every `global_configs` entry in `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` can declare the environment variables that relocate its own config file (`config_env "VAR"` children), parsed into a new `ClientIntegrationGlobalConfig::config_env: Vec<String>`; entries whose file has no relocation variable declare an empty list. | Implemented: the `config_env` field and parser arm in `rust/src/seed/client_integrations.rs`, filled in `data/seed/client-integrations.lino` (and its committed `rust/embedded/` mirror) only where in-repo evidence exists. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1161_client_registry_env.rs`. |
| R1161-2 | `agent` names `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG` (config file) and `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR` (directory); `codex` and the `t3code` OpenAI-protocol entry name `CODEX_HOME`; `opencode`, `opencode-vscode` and `opencode-desktop` name `OPENCODE_CONFIG` and `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`. | Implemented in the same seed file. Evidence per client: agent — the issue itself and the wrapper's own `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_CONTENT` one-shot mechanism; codex — `docs/configuration/output-sessions.md` (`$CODEX_HOME/sessions/…`), `experiments/agentic_cli_matrix/README.md` (`CODEX_HOME` → a directory holding `config.toml`) and `rust/tests/issue_760.rs`; t3code — its own ephemeral block relocates the same `config.toml` via `CODEX_HOME` (`docs/configuration/t3-code.md`); opencode family — each block's own ephemeral `config_env "OPENCODE_CONFIG"` / `config_dir_env "OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR"`. Pinned by the per-client assertions in the same test file. |
| R1161-3 | The declaration is a registry surface: `formal-ai clients --format json` carries it additively as `global_configs[].config_env` (plus the one-shot `config_env`/`config_dir_env`/`config_content_env`/`temp_home_env` top-level fields), and `formal-ai clients` prints it on each `global[...]` line. | Implemented in `rust/src/cli_clients.rs`. Additive only — the matrix (`experiments/agentic_cli_matrix/run_leg.sh`) still reads exactly the `verification.*` fields it read before. The projection is a bin module and is reviewed, not unit-tested; the underlying parsed data is what the test pins. |
| R1161-4 | A host integration contract is documented: a host that needs a task-local client config sets the declared variable and must not relocate `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `HOME` (the 2026-09-27 `gh`-auth incident, link-assistant/hive-mind#2314). | Implemented: the "Host integration contract" section and the *Relocate via* column in `docs/configuration/agentic-clis.md`, the registry-surface note in `docs/testing/agentic-cli-tools.md`. |
| R1161-5 | Clients whose global entry is a shell profile (`gemini`, `claude`, `qwen`, `aider`) or a fixed path with no evidenced variable (`cursor`, `grok`) declare none; no variable is fabricated. | Implemented and pinned by `entries_without_a_relocation_variable_declare_none` in the same test file. |
| R1161-6 | Hive Mind switches its Formal AI agent launcher from the `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` relocation to `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR`/`LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG`. | Cross-repo (link-assistant/hive-mind#2314): this repository's part — naming the variables as registry data and documenting the contract — is delivered here; the launcher change itself is tracked in the Hive Mind repository and is not confirmed from this repo. |
| R1161-7 | The declared relocation actually works end to end: the agent CLI is started with `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG(_DIR)` pointing at a temporary config directory and serves the session from it (pull-request follow-up row: the smoke test half of the registry surface). | Implemented in CI, pending its first matrix run: `case_relocated` in `experiments/agentic_cli_matrix/run_leg.sh` runs for every headless CLI client whose global config declares `config_env`. It writes the config with `formal-ai with --globally` into a scratch home, copies the written directory to a temporary one, and starts the real CLI directly. The run uses an empty `HOME` and only one declared variable, which points at the copied directory (`*_DIR`/`*_HOME`) or file (the others). The case asserts that the session reaches `formal-ai serve` through the recording proxy and that nothing is written back into `HOME`. For `agent` this runs `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG` and `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_CONFIG_DIR`. Pinned by `the_matrix_leg_serves_a_session_from_each_declared_relocation_variable`. The `agentic-cli-matrix.yml` legs confirm it on the next run. |

## Issue #1163 Internet as Formal Knowledge

Issue [#1163](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1163) (E128,
part of the #1183 umbrella) turns fetched web pages into formal knowledge: one
generic page formalizer maps any fetched resource to a `LinkNetwork` (headings,
paragraphs, lists, tables, and language-tagged code blocks), search becomes the
entry point for a need no registered source covers, pages carry a data-driven
trust score and a rediscovery record, and queries over formalized pages answer
with links. The issue numbers its requirements 1 to 10; they are
`R1163-1` to `R1163-10` here in the same order. `R1163-11` to `R1163-16` are
the further obligations its "What to build", "How to test", "Design" and
"Definition of done" sections state without a number. The timeline, root
causes and prior art live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1163/`.

The module is `rust/src/web_formalize.rs` (with `rust/src/web_formalize_trust.rs`
included from it), not the `rust/src/page_formalizer.rs` the issue names; the
four test modules the issue sketches are consolidated in
`rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_web_formalize.rs`. The browser twin is
`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_web_formalize.js`, tested by
`rust/tests/web/issue-1163-web-formalize-parity.test.mjs`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1163-1 | A single `formalize_page(bytes, mime_hint) -> LinkNetwork` produces a `LinkNetwork` from any HTML, Markdown, plain-text, JSON, or PDF-text payload. | Implemented: `web_formalize::formalize_page` resolves the mime kind from the hint or the seed's sniff rules (`data/seed/page-formalization-rules.lino`) and builds a `page` root with one `heading` / `paragraph` / `list_item` / `table_row` / `code_block` child per block. Pinned by `html_page_formalizes_structure_and_code`, `markdown_fences_tag_languages_with_unknown_fallback`, `generic_formalizer_covers_bespoke_statements` (JSON) and `plain_and_pdf_text_formalize` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_web_formalize.rs`. The HTML walker once stepped over the whole document (an `<html>` open tag jumped the cursor past `</html>`) and the rule loaders once read no records (they iterated the top level, which holds only the file wrapper); both are fixed on this branch and the HTML test fails if either returns. Note: the network is assembled by inserting links, not by `LinkNetwork::parse`, and bare source files take the plain-text path. |
| R1163-2 | Every code block carries a language tag from the fence annotation, the HTML class, or a heuristic; an unrecognized fence yields `unknown`, never an empty tag. | Implemented: `resolve_language` walks the seed's `tag_source` order (fence, `html_class` with the seed's `language-` and `highlight ` class prefixes, the latter reading GitHub-style `highlight-source-<x>`, shebang and URL-extension heuristic) and falls back to the seed's `unknown`. Pinned by `markdown_fences_tag_languages_with_unknown_fallback` (fences `rust` and `shell`, bare fence `unknown`), `scala_page_tags_language_through_class_prefix`, `html_page_formalizes_structure_and_code` and `heuristic_tier_tags_unannotated_fences` (shebang `python`, URL extension `rust`) in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_web_formalize.rs`, and in the browser twin by the fence, class and heuristic tests of `rust/tests/web/issue-1163-web-formalize-parity.test.mjs`. The Rust tests named here were drafted on 2026-10-07 without a local cargo run; CI is their first verification. Gap: an annotated fence the seed does not know (for example a made-up tag) passes through verbatim rather than becoming `unknown`, and the URL-extension tier matches a suffix anywhere in the URL (`.c` would match `.com`), so it relies on the seed's row order. |
| R1163-3 | For each of the six bespoke extractors, `formalize_page` on the same fixture bytes yields every statement the bespoke extractor yields (generic ⊇ bespoke). | Implemented on fixtures: `concept_lookup::extractor_statements` exposes what each of the six bespoke extractors yields (the four lexical readers through `read_glosses`, `oeis_sequence_v1` through the new `oeis::record_statements`, `python_docs_v1` through `python_docs::page_statements`, which now shares `page_definitions` with the index builder), and `generic_formalizer_covers_every_bespoke_extractor` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_formal_knowledge_paths.rs` pins each extractor's real output exactly on its own fixture under `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1163/<extractor>/` and checks the generic network covers it; `wiktionary_entry_v1` keeps its earlier test. The HTML walker gained `<dt>` as a list item so a reference page's signature line is a statement (mirrored in the browser twin). The Rust tests named here were drafted on 2026-10-07 without a local cargo run; CI is their first verification; the JavaScript twins are verified locally by `rust/tests/web/issue-1163-formal-knowledge-paths.test.mjs` (5 tests). Gap: the five new fixtures are hand-trimmed payloads in each API's shape, not byte captures, and the bespoke Python reader inserts a space at every inline tag where the generic walker does not, so pages with inline markup inside a signature compare only modulo whitespace. |
| R1163-4 | A need whose `need_kinds` match nothing in `data/seed/sources-registry.lino` routes to web search through the existing RRF pipeline instead of returning empty. | Implemented: `RegistrySourceLookup::lookup` (the `SourceLookup` the need-satisfaction loop `formalization::needs::satisfy` asks) now sends a need whose kind no registry row declares to `research_unmatched_need`, ranks the captured pages with `pages_by_trust` and reads each through the registry row whose extractor is `generic_page_v1`, so every sense carries the page URL, SHA-256 and that row's license and tier. Pinned by `unmatched_need_is_satisfied_through_web_research` (a `decision` need for `compiler` is satisfied from the kotlinlang page's three mentioning statements) in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_formal_knowledge_paths.rs`, beside `unmatched_need_routes_to_web_search`. The Rust tests named here were drafted on 2026-10-07 without a local cargo run; CI is their first verification; the JavaScript twins are verified locally by `rust/tests/web/issue-1163-formal-knowledge-paths.test.mjs` (5 tests). Gap: only `decision` is unclaimed by the registry today, and no prompt-level planner raises a `decision` need yet. |
| R1163-5 | Each web-search result is fetched through `CachedSourceClient`, its `sha256` and `fetched_at` are recorded, and its bytes are passed to `formalize_page`. | Implemented: `execute_source_research` fetches every fused result through `CachedSourceClient`, and `SourceResearchExecution::learning_proposal` formalizes each captured page's bytes and emits one `formalized_page_statement` record per statement, carrying the URL and SHA-256, beside the `source_observation` record (URL, `fetched_at`, SHA-256). Pinned by `source_research_formalizes_pages_into_working_memory` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_web_formalize.rs`, which counts one record per statement of the captured kotlinlang page and finds its hash and heading. The Rust tests named here were drafted on 2026-10-07 without a local cargo run; CI is their first verification. |
| R1163-6 | The formalized network is stored in the solver's working memory under a key encoding the URL and SHA-256, so a second solve for the same URL reuses it without a re-fetch. | Implemented: a formalized page now keeps its capture, and `execute_source_research` asks `web_formalize::remembered_capture` before `client.fetch`, so a URL already in working memory is replayed from memory (as a cache hit with the original timestamp and digest, `SourceCapture::replayed`) and never fetched. Pinned by `store_keys_pages_by_url_and_hash` and `source_research_formalizes_pages_into_working_memory` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_web_formalize.rs` and by `research_consults_working_memory_before_fetching` (a second research through an empty cache and a transport refusing every page still yields the page) in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_formal_knowledge_paths.rs`; the browser store's `formalizedPageStoreCapture` is its twin. The Rust tests named here were drafted on 2026-10-07 without a local cargo run; CI is their first verification; the JavaScript twins are verified locally by `rust/tests/web/issue-1163-formal-knowledge-paths.test.mjs` (5 tests). Gap: the memory is per thread, not persisted, and a remembered page is reused until the thread ends rather than until its capture's TTL. |
| R1163-7 | A trust score in [0, 1] is computed from data-held weights (official website via Wikidata P856, HTTPS, registry `primacy`, open license, cross-page agreement); it ranks sources and never excludes one. | Implemented: `trust_features_for` computes every feature: HTTPS from the URL, the primacy grade of the registered source on the same domain, an open license from the seed's `license_marker` strings, agreement from stored pages on other domains that state one of the page's paragraphs or code blocks, and the official site from the P856 claims `official_websites` reads out of a Wikidata entity payload (the property is the seed's `claim_property`). `remember_capture` scores every researched page this way, and `SourceResearchExecution::pages_by_trust` orders captured pages by that score without dropping any. Pinned by `trust_score_ranks_without_excluding` and by `trust_features_are_computed_from_the_page` (official site, HTTPS and one agreeing mirror score 48; the Python docs page grades `self_published`; a Creative Commons link is an open license; a researched kotlinlang page is stored at 10) in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_formal_knowledge_paths.rs`, with `pageTrustFeatures` and `pageOfficialWebsites` as browser twins. The Rust tests named here were drafted on 2026-10-07 without a local cargo run; CI is their first verification; the JavaScript twins are verified locally by `rust/tests/web/issue-1163-formal-knowledge-paths.test.mjs` (5 tests). Gap: the search path holds no Wikidata entity for the page's subject, so it scores the official-site feature unset; only the concept-walk ordering of R1163-4 consumes the ranking. |
| R1163-8 | The memory query language resolves "code blocks on `<domain>` whose text contains `<term>`" and "the command in the paragraph that mentions `<phrase>`" against formalized pages and returns `Link` values. | Implemented: both surfaces are templates (`page_query` records) in `data/seed/page-formalization-rules.lino`, parsed by `memory_query_language::parse_page_query` and run by `run_page_query` (or `run_page_query_in_working_memory`) against `FormalizedPageStore::code_blocks_on` and `FormalizedPageStore::command_mentioning`, which return `Vec<Link>`. `command_mentioning` now answers only for paragraphs that themselves mention the phrase, each with the command tied to it (the paragraph when it is a command, else the code block or command paragraph it introduces). Pinned by `page_queries_answer_with_links` (the compiling query yields the kotlinc block, not the `java -jar` paragraph) and `memory_query_language_resolves_page_queries` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1163_web_formalize.rs`, and by `formalizedPageQuery` in `rust/tests/web/issue-1163-web-formalize-parity.test.mjs`. The Rust tests named here were drafted on 2026-10-07 without a local cargo run; CI is their first verification. ## Issue #1164 Code Node Decomposition

Issue [#1164](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1164) (E129,
part of the #1183 umbrella) makes retrieved code examples formal knowledge: an
example is parsed into the meta language, decomposed into meaningful parts
(entry point, output operation, string literal, import, build and run
commands), generalized across languages by aligning those parts, and
recomposed for a new requirement. The issue states `R1164-1` to `R1164-11`;
`R1164-12` to `R1164-15` are the further obligations of its "Tests" and
"Definition of done" sections. The timeline, root causes and prior art live in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1164/`.

The module is `rust/src/code_example_knowledge.rs`, not the
`rust/src/coding/code_node_decomposer.rs` the issue names; the two test
modules the issue sketches are consolidated in
`rust/tests/unit/issue_1164_code_example_knowledge.rs`. The part vocabulary
is data in `data/seed/code-example-parts.lino`, which stores no program text:
recomposition builds from the decomposed examples. The browser twin is
`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_code_examples.js`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1164-1 | `decompose_code_node` returns `DecomposeError::UnknownGrammar(<slug>)` for a slug with no entry in `data/seed/program-cst-grammars.lino`; it never guesses. | Implemented: the grammar lookup through `coding::cst::grammar_metadata` runs before anything else. Pinned by `unknown_grammar_slug_returns_unknown_grammar_error` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1164_code_example_knowledge.rs` (`zig` and `pascal` both refused by name). |
| R1164-2 | For every registered slug, `decompose_code_node` parses through `LinkNetwork::parse` and returns at least one output operation, string literal, and entry point where the language has one. | Implemented: the parse goes through `LinkNetwork::parse` with the seed's grammar label; `decompose_rust_hello_world_produces_entry_output_literal`, `decompose_go_hello_world_produces_entry_output_literal`, `decompose_python_script_has_no_entry_point`, `every_captured_fixture_decomposes` and `registered_languages_decompose_output_and_literal` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1164_code_example_knowledge.rs` check the output operation and literal for all fifteen registered slugs (rust, go, python, kotlin, swift, scala, javascript, typescript, java, csharp, c, cpp, ruby, php, r), and `r` now has a `part_language` row in the seed. The Rust tests named here were drafted on 2026-10-07 without a local cargo run; CI is their first verification. Gap: the entry point is asserted only for rust, go and kotlin. |

## Issue #1165 Discovery on the Production Path

Issue [#1165](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1165) (E130)
puts the coding-by-discovery machinery on the path users and Hive Mind hit:
every stored program becomes a *cache entry* that names where a rediscovery
starts from, a cache miss routes to `research_coding_skill_gap` instead of a
template literal, and the whole cache is deletable by design. The analysis
and the wiring plan live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1165/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1165-1 | When the solver selects `SelectedRule::WriteProgram` and no cached procedure exists for the language/task, `research_coding_skill_gap` runs on the miss path and the answer is discovery-backed. | Partial (2026-10-07, this pull request): the `WriteProgram` branch of `rust/src/solver.rs` loads the procedure cache and calls `discovery_production::cached_write_program`; a verified row for the `(language, task)` pair replaces the catalog template in both the answer and the `ExecutionRecipe`, with a `procedure_cache` hit event in the derivation, and a prompt that customised the template keeps its own program. Pinned by `write_program_reuses_the_cached_procedure_only_for_an_unmodified_request` (Rust and JS). The miss path now names its gap instead of hiding it: the policy seed `data/seed/program-cache-policy.lino` gains a `miss_route` record (research requires `expected_output` and `reviewer_approval`; a solve carries `expected_output`), `discovery_production::miss_research_missing` (JS twin `missResearchMissing`) reads it, and an unmodified request with no cache row logs `procedure_cache outcome=miss language=... task=... research_missing=reviewer_approval`. Pinned by `miss_route_names_what_research_lacks_on_a_solve` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1165_discovery_production.rs` (drafted without a local cargo run) and its JS twin. Open: research itself does not run on a solve, because no solve call carries a reviewer's `CodingResearchApproval`; the answer on a miss is still the template. |
| R1165-2 | `plan_work_item_execution` replaces a template-backed `execution_recipe` through the same miss path; `planned_not_executed` is never emitted for a recognised pair. | Partial (2026-10-07, this pull request): `plan_work_item_execution` takes its `execution_recipe` from the solver's answer, so it inherits the cache-backed recipe of R1165-1 and the named miss gap in the same derivation. Open: on a miss it still executes the template recipe, for the reason R1165-1 names (no reviewer approval on the solve path). `planned_not_executed` is unchanged. |
| R1165-3 | A stored procedure is accepted only when its gap records a `rediscovery_query` and a `rediscovery_source`. | Implemented: `ProcedureCache::store` refuses rows without both fields (`store_rejects_procedure_without_rediscovery_fields`), and the policy seed `data/seed/program-cache-policy.lino` declares the requirement as data read by the module. |
| R1165-4 | `hello-world-programs.lino` and `ORACLE_SNAPSHOTS` are deleted; `knows_language` becomes "a grammar exists and discovery found a procedure". | Partial: `rust/src/knowledge.rs` gates every snapshot answer on `bootstrap_cache_active()`, which reads the policy seed, so retiring the bootstrap is a seed edit. `discovery_production::knows_language` implements the grammar-plus-procedure reading: kotlin answers, and rust does not until its row exists. Open (re-checked 2026-10-07): deleting `hello-world-programs.lino` and `ORACLE_SNAPSHOTS` now would remove the only answer for the bootstrap languages (`bootstrap_tier_is_governed_by_the_policy_seed` pins kotlin) while the cache ships with no rows. The deletion has to follow the rediscovery run that writes those rows (R1165-7). The registry, `solver_handler_oracle.rs`, `behavior_rules.rs` and the `rust/tests/source` mirrors are the call sites. Re-checked in a second pass (2026-10-07): the `ORACLE_SNAPSHOTS` rows carry an `expected_output`, but a cache row's `verified_output` means `research_coding_skill_gap` ran the program and matched it under an approval, and none of the snapshot languages (kotlin, swift, php, bash, lua, haskell) was executed; copying the snapshots into the cache as "verified" rows would be memorization with a verification label, and would also raise the R1165-8 ratchet by the copied programs. Deletion therefore still waits for real rows. |
| R1165-5 | `entry`/`operation`/`ci_setup`/`documented_source` move from `stdout-program-contracts.lino` into the new cache format with a `rediscovery_query` per row. | Format delivered: `data/cache/coding-procedure-cache.lino` carries exactly those fields plus `rediscovery_query`/`rediscovery_source`/`content_id`. The reader/writer round-trip is pinned by `store_lookup_reload_roundtrip`. Open (re-checked 2026-10-07): `coding::program_contract::answer` (and its JS twin) still builds every program from the `entry`/`operation`/`ci_setup` fields of `stdout-program-contracts.lino`, and the cache holds no rows to replace them, so pruning the fields now would delete the program-contract path. The `ci_setup` values themselves are placeholders only since R1168-6. Re-checked in a second pass (2026-10-07): unchanged, the cache still has no verified rows to take these fields over. |
| R1165-6 | No language row hard-codes a compile command once a verified procedure reproduces it. | Open: no verified procedure exists yet to reproduce a compile command, because the cache ships with no rows. `rust/src/coding/catalog/languages.rs` is still owned by the meta-language slice (#1167). The cache format can carry the reproduced check command (`verified_output`), and the deletion lands after the rediscovery run. Re-checked in a second pass (2026-10-07): unchanged, for the reason R1165-4 records. |
| R1165-7 | A test deletes the entire cache and proves `research_coding_skill_gap` recreates rows with the same `content_id` for six languages including grammar-covered Pascal. | Offline half delivered: `delete_all_empties_the_cache_file` plus `content_id_is_fnv1a_of_entry_and_recomputed_on_store` (FNV-1a of the program bytes, recomputed on store, drift rejected on load). Writing that test blind, without a live run to confirm it, would only pin a guess. Re-checked in a second pass (2026-10-07): the Pascal leg now has its grammar row and a documented source (R1164-9 decomposes the Free Pascal Quick Start example), but the six-language research run still needs a live fetch and an approval set per language. |

## Issue #1166 The Request Formalized into Obligations

Issue [#1166](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1166) (E131)
replaces phrase matching with request formalization: an issue body parses
into an obligation graph whose nodes carry semantic kinds and anchored
literals, mentions of the same quoted literal collapse to one node (the
structural fix for the Kotlin doubled output of #1156), and nothing
underivable is silently discarded. The root-cause analysis lives in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1166/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1166-1 | An issue body parses into an `ObligationGraph`; every enumerated requirement produces an `ObligationNode` anchored to seed meanings/roles. | Implemented: `rust/src/intent_formalization/obligations.rs` (`formalize_request`) builds on `obligation_ledger::ObligationNode::build` — no new ledger type — and classifies clauses against `print_stdout`, `ci_workflow_request`, and the program-request roles. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs`. |
| R1166-2 | Two or more mentions of the same quoted literal produce exactly one output-literal node. | Implemented: `coreference_pass` merges by literal value across clauses; `two_identical_output_clauses_produce_one_node` proves three mentions (intro, "print exactly", Expected Output) yield one node and one value. |
| R1166-3 | The executor derives its plan from obligation nodes and reports undischargeable nodes with byte spans. | Partial (2026-10-07, this pull request). The graph exposes `obligations_of_kind` and `gap_report` (node id + byte span + reason). The executor's CI-workflow decision comes from the graph: `ci_workflow::requested_in` delegates to `intent_formalization::request_demands(objective, ObligationKind::CiWorkflow)`, and its JS twin `requestedIn` (`js/agentic/ci_workflow.mjs`) reads the same clause nodes (`ci_workflow_demand_is_read_from_the_obligation_graph`, Rust and JS). The program-contract executor (`coding::program_contract::answer`) now calls the new `intent_formalization::record_obligation_gaps`, which writes one `obligation_gap` event per `gap_report` line into the run's log, so the derivation trace carries every clause it could not read; pinned by `undischargeable_clauses_are_recorded_in_the_run` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1166_obligation_routing.rs` (drafted without a local cargo run; the JS twin builds no trace, so the emission is native-only). Open: `program_contract::explicit_stdout` still reads print clauses itself. The graph's `OutputLiteral` reading is broader (it uses the fallback verb tables and takes the last quoted segment of a clause), and adopting it changes which prompts get a program contract, so that needs its own parity pass. |
| R1166-4 | A completed run emits an obligation report for each undischargeable node; none is silently omitted. | Delivered at module level, and on the program-contract path since 2026-10-07: `ObligationGraph::gap_report` and `underivable()`, emitted by `record_obligation_gaps` as `obligation_gap` events (see R1166-3). Other executors do not emit them yet. Re-checked 2026-10-07 and deliberately left open: routing `program_contract::explicit_stdout` through the graph's `OutputLiteral` nodes (the R1166-3 rewrite) changes which prompts get a program contract, because the graph reading uses the fallback verb tables and takes a clause's last quoted segment, so it is a routing change with cross-runtime parity impact (Rust `explicit_stdout` and its JS twin, plus the parity corpus), not a local edit; it needs its own parity pass. |
| R1166-5 | An underivable clause yields `ObligationExpectation::Underivable`, split or reported, never discarded. | Implemented and pinned: `unknown_requirement_clause_yields_underivable_node_not_panic` (the ledger's own expectation semantics; the classifier leaves such nodes unclassified). |
| R1166-6 | A translated body (en/ru/hi/zh/es) yields the same graph modulo the language tag. | Implemented for the fixture family: `kotlin_issue_ru_yields_same_obligation_count_as_en` and `kotlin_issue_hi_zh_es_yield_same_graph_modulo_language_tag` over `rust/tests/fixtures/issue-1166/hello-world-kotlin-{en,ru,hi,zh,es}.txt`; classification reads the seed lexicon's multilingual lexemes with documented per-language fallback tables for the style/naming/badge vocabulary the seeds do not own yet. |
| R1166-7 | A paraphrased body produces an equivalent graph. | Implemented: `paraphrase_en_yields_same_obligation_count_as_canonical_en` over `hello-world-kotlin-paraphrase-en.txt`. |
| R1166-8 | Routing decides by the formalized request, not the leading word. | Implemented for the terminal router: `leading_shell_command` in `rust/src/solver_terminal.rs` now consults `request_carries_work_obligations` — a quoted output literal plus an authoring clause (program, CI, style, naming, badge) is a sentence about building something, in any of the five languages, while `git status` and `echo "Hello, World!"` stay commands (`work_obligation_requests_are_not_terminal_commands`). |

## Issue #1168 Generated Code Uses Versions Resolved at Generation Time

Issue [#1168](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1168) (E133)
makes every third-party version a generated artifact pins — action refs,
toolchain versions, the Java LTS — a *resolved* value with provenance, never a
memorized string. Resolution happens at generation time from the publisher's
own API, is recorded in the derivation, and degrades loudly (cache, then
shipped baseline, each said out loud) rather than silently going stale.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1168-1 | The latest release tag and its commit SHA for every third-party GitHub Action in a generated CI workflow are fetched from `https://api.github.com/repos/{publisher}/{repo}/releases/latest` (then `commits/{tag}` for the SHA). | Implemented: `resolve_github` in `rust/src/version_resolution.rs`, covering `actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-java`, `fwilhe2/setup-kotlin`, `actions/setup-python`; pinned by mocked-transport tests (`resolves_every_pin_from_live_fixtures`). |
| R1168-2 | The Kotlin version is the latest `JetBrains/kotlin` release tag. | Implemented in the same module (`v2.4.20` as shipped baseline); the tag feeds `fwilhe2/setup-kotlin`'s `version:` argument through `fill_workflow_versions`. |
| R1168-3 | The Java version is Adoptium's own `most_recent_lts`, never a literal `'21'`. | Implemented: `resolve_java_lts` reads `https://api.adoptium.net/v3/info/available_releases` (25 as shipped baseline). |
| R1168-4 | Every resolved version is recorded in the derivation as a `SourceCapture` (source_url, fetched_at, sha256, cached, bytes) via the existing `CachedSourceClient`. | Implemented: `VersionSet::record` appends each capture's provenance plus one `version_resolution` line per pin; pinned by `records_the_resolution_in_the_derivation`. |
| R1168-5 | When the live API is unreachable, the most recent cached capture is used and the answer is annotated `(version resolved from cache; fetched_at=<timestamp>)`. | Implemented: `CachedSourceClient` replay supplies `Origin::Cache`, and `provenance_note` emits exactly that wording — extended to the shipped baseline, which annotates `(version resolved from the shipped baseline measured <date>)`; `ci_workflow::render` prepends the notes as workflow comments. Pinned by `offline_replays_the_cached_capture_and_says_so`. |
| R1168-6 | `workflow_template` and `ci_setup` values carry placeholders, never literal SHAs or bare versions. | Implemented (2026-10-07, this pull request). `fill_workflow_versions` fills `{checkout_ref}` … `{java_lts}` plus the new `{setup_coursier_ref}`/`{setup_coursier_tag}`/`{scala_version}`, and still rewrites any stale `@<sha>` / `version: '…'` literal that slips through, scoped per action block. The last literal template row is gone: the Scala `ci_setup` in `data/meta/stdout-program-contracts.lino` (and its embedded mirror) now reads `coursier/setup-action@{setup_coursier_ref} # {setup_coursier_tag}`, `jvm: temurin:{java_lts}` and `apps: scala:{scala_version} scalac:{scala_version}`. `VersionSet` resolves `coursier/setup-action` and `scala/scala` (shipped baselines v3.0.4 @ 648df969… and 2.13.18, measured 2026-10-07 from the GitHub releases API, in `data/seed/toolchains.lino`). `work-item-steps.lino` already carried placeholders only. Pinned by `fills_the_scala_ci_setup_placeholders` and `repository_data_carries_no_memorized_pin`. |
| R1168-7 | A CI gate fails on any `@<sha>` or bare version literal for a third-party action or toolchain in `data/`. | Implemented: `scripts/check-generated-version-literals.rs` (scans `data/` minus `data/cache/`; the toolchains baseline is exempt by shape, not by name), with embedded tests plus `rust/tests/unit/issue_1168_latest_versions.rs`, where `repository_data_carries_no_memorized_pin` now asserts zero findings in the repository's `data/`. The gate is registered as a CI stage in `data/meta/ci-gates/check-generated-version-literals.lino` (stage `rust`). |
| R1168-8 | Three-roots parity: `version_resolution.rs` translated to js/ts and parity cases added. | Partial (2026-10-07, this pull request). JS root: `js/agentic/crate/version_resolution.mjs` mirrors `VersionSet::resolve` (`resolveVersionSet`, over an injected `fetch` that stands in for `CachedSourceClient`, with the same live → cache → baseline ladder and capture order), `VersionSet::record` (`recordVersionSet`), the coursier/Scala pins, and now `VersionSet::for_generation`: `forGeneration(fetch)` walks the same ladder over a host-supplied `fetch` and answers from the shipped baseline when the host passes none. `rust/tests/web/issue-1168-version-resolution-parity.test.mjs` reproduces the Rust cases and adds `for_generation_walks_live_then_cache_then_baseline` (6 tests, passing locally). TS root: `ts/agentic/crate/version_resolution.mts` is generated by `scripts/translate-es.mjs`. Open: no JavaScript host owns a source cache yet, so its callers (`coding_program_contract.mjs`, `ci_workflow.mjs`) still call `forGeneration()` without a fetch, and there are no `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` cases, because the browser worker does not answer the program-contract prompts whose workflows carry the pins. |

The shipped baseline in `data/seed/toolchains.lino` (`generated_version` records)
was measured 2026-09-30 against the live APIs and tags: checkout `v7.0.1`
(`3d3c42e5…`), setup-java `v6.0.1` (`de7274f0…`), setup-kotlin `v2.0`
(`ee96925…`), setup-python `v7.0.0` (`5fda3b95…`), CPython `3.14.7`, Kotlin
`v2.4.20`, Java LTS `25`; coursier/setup-action `v3.0.4` (`648df969…`) and
Scala `2.13.18` were added 2026-10-07 from the same releases API.

## Issue #1169 Every Dependency at Its Latest Release

Issue [#1169](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1169) (E134)
makes dependency currency a fact the repository enforces, not a habit it
hopes for: every dependency — crates, npm packages, GitHub Action refs, the
container base image, the rustc floor — sits at its publisher's latest
release, and a gate fails when one does not. The one sanctioned hold-back is
an in-tree annotation naming the issue that tracks it.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1169-1 | A gate reads every ecosystem the repository declares: `rust/Cargo.toml` against `rust/Cargo.lock`, every `package.json` against its lockfile (manifest-range fallback where a directory ships no lock), `uses:` refs in `.github/workflows` and composite actions, `FROM` bases in the `Dockerfile`, and the `rust-version` floor. | Implemented: `collect` in `scripts/check-dependencies-latest.rs`, walking with `node_modules`/`target`/`.git`/`.claude`/`cache` excluded; pinned by `the_repository_tree_collects_every_ecosystem` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1169_dependency_currency.rs`. |
| R1169-2 | "Latest" comes from the publisher's own registry — crates.io `max_stable_version`, npm `dist-tags.latest`, GitHub `releases/latest`, Docker Hub tags, the rust stable channel — never a memorized list. | Implemented: the `latest_*` fetchers (curl + `USER_AGENT`, 30 s cap), each parsed from the publisher's own answer. |
| R1169-3 | A dependency may be held back only with a same-line annotation naming the tracking issue; the gate verifies the annotation, and drift without one fails. | Implemented: `blocked_annotation` requires `# blocked: <https://…/issues/…>` in Cargo.toml and a `"<name>//"` sibling key in package.json; blocked findings are reported with `(blocked)` and do not fail, unblocked drift exits 1. Documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md` beside the self-maintained-dependencies policy. `links-notation = "0.16.1" # blocked: …` is the first resident: lino-objects-codec 0.7.0 requires `^0.16`. |
| R1169-4 | The tree itself is moved to latest: `cargo update` resolution (already applied to `rust/Cargo.lock` — command-stream 1.2.0, webrtc 0.21.0, toml_edit 0.25.15, clap 4.6.7 …), npm manifests hand-bumped with real registry integrity (react/react-dom 19.3.0, dompurify 3.4.16, marked 18.0.14, command-stream 1.2.0, electron 44.4.5, electron-builder 26.17.0 with its app-builder-lib/dmg-builder/builder-util/electron-publish/squirrel-windows ring, playwright 1.63.0 across desktop + e2e + vscode), and the pin edits (`konrad/box-dind` 2.10.2, `actions/cache` v6 in both composite actions, `zizmor-action` v0.6.4). | Implemented (re-checked 2026-10-07, this pull request). The listed moves are in the tree: `rust/Cargo.lock` resolves command-stream 1.2.0, webrtc 0.21.0, toml_edit 0.25.15 and clap 4.6.7; `package.json` pins react/react-dom 19.3.0, dompurify 3.4.16 and marked 18.0.14; `desktop/package.json` pins command-stream 1.2.0, electron ^44.4.5, electron-builder ^26.17.0 and playwright ^1.63.0; vscode and `rust/tests/e2e` pin playwright ^1.63.0 with their locks; `Dockerfile` runs `FROM konard/box-dind:2.10.2`; all three composite actions use `actions/cache@v6`; `zizmor-action@v0.6.4`. The desktop/e2e lock edits were verified closed by a before/after range-resolution diff over the `packages` map. The stale `konard/box-dind:2.1.1` comments in `Dockerfile.slim` and `container-images.yml` now name 2.10.2. The desktop and VS Code sandbox image now name `konard/box-dind:2.10.2` too (verified on Docker Hub as the current tag, published for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64): `desktop/lib/tool-router.cjs` `SANDBOX_IMAGE`, `desktop/scripts/smoke.mjs`, `vscode/src/lib/config.cjs` `DEFAULT_IMAGE`, the `vscode/package.json` setting default, the `docker_microservice` environment of `data/seed/environments.lino` (embedded mirror too), README, `vscode/README.md` and the architecture/desktop/vscode docs, with `docker_runtime.rs`, `docs_requirements.rs` and `formal_ai_cli.rs` pinning 2.10.2. The one remaining 2.1.1 pin is the historical issue #195 case-study research note, which records what was true then. No desktop or VS Code smoke run against the new image was recorded locally; the pinning tests run in CI. |
| R1169-5 | A daily job refreshes the registry answers, applies every unblocked bump, re-resolves lockfiles, re-runs the CI gates, and opens one PR with whatever moved. | Implemented: `.github/workflows/dependencies-latest.yml` (cron `23 5 * * *`, off the fleet's :00 stampede per issue #1021) — `--refresh-snapshot`, `--apply --offline`, `cargo update --workspace`, `bun install` per manifest directory, `run-ci-gates` all three stages, `peter-evans/create-pull-request@v8`. Not yet run (needs CI). |
| R1169-6 | Registry flakiness never reddens CI: `--offline` answers from `data/meta/dependency-registry-snapshot.lino`, written by `--refresh-snapshot`; an unreachable registry exits 3, distinct from findings. | Implemented: `read_snapshot`/`write_snapshot` (flat lino, one `registry_entry <ecosystem>/<name>` record per answer) and the exit-code ladder 0/1/2/3 in `main`. |
| R1169-7 | `--apply` moves manifests (not lockfiles) and leaves annotated pins alone; lockfiles are re-derived by the daily job's resolvers. | Implemented: `apply_latest` + the per-ecosystem line rewriters; pinned by `apply_moves_unblocked_manifests_and_leaves_blocked_alone`. |
| R1169-8 | The gate's parsers and rules are pinned by tests that compile the script into the unit suite. | Implemented: eleven embedded tests in the script plus three fixture-tree tests in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1169_dependency_currency.rs` (`#[path]` include, the `ci_gates.rs` idiom). |

Residuals for the integrating commit: the unit-suite registration line in
`rust/tests/unit/mod.rs` (shared wiring, deliberately untouched here), the
`data/meta/ci-gates/` registration shard, and the first
`--refresh-snapshot` run to seed `data/meta/dependency-registry-snapshot.lino`
(all under the parent's `data/meta`/shared-wiring ownership). The gate is
expected to run red on first CI invocation for legacy pins it newly
surfaces — most `uses:` refs across `.github/workflows` predate this gate
and carry no blocked annotation; the daily job's first PR is the designed
way they move.

VS Code packaging residual: `@vscode/vsce` remains at `^3.9.2`, matching
`vscode/package-lock.json`. This is an unresolved dependency currency gap. Publisher
metadata for 4.0.0 requires Node >=22 and a changed dependency graph, including
`@napi-rs/keyring`, `@vscode/vsce-sign` ^2.1.0, and Secretlint core/types/source
creator packages. Complete this bump in CI with a full npm lockfile resolution;
replacing the top-level package version alone would leave missing dependencies.
Playwright and playwright-core are updated together to 1.63.0 in that lockfile,
using the same registry integrity records as the e2e lockfile. No builds or tests
were run for these integration changes.

## Issue #1172 Factual QA Subject-Verified Lookup

Issue [#1172](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1172) (E137,
part of the #1183 umbrella) reports that "What is the capital of Australia?"
was answered with "The capital of the United States is Washington, D.C." —
the alias "us" matched as a raw substring inside "a**us**tralia". A wrong
answer is worse than no answer. This shard pins the delivered word-boundary
fix (R1, R4, R10, R11 of the issue), the subject Q-id gate (R2), seeded
comparisons (R6), questions over prompt-supplied text (R7) and the shared
parity case (R1172-12), and records the open follow-ups (R3, R5, R8, R9 and
the live-data halves of R6/R7) honestly. The root-cause
analysis, the corrected issue-0127 rows, and
the evidence live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1172/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1172-1 | A subject alias or question keyword may match the normalized prompt only at word boundaries (tokenized comparison), never as a raw substring inside a longer word: "us" must not match inside "australia"; multi-word aliases ("united states") match as consecutive token sequences; CJK surfaces, which have no inter-word spaces, keep substring matching. | Implemented: `FactRecord::matches_normalized` (`rust/src/seed/facts.rs`) now gates every alias and keyword through the new associated `FactRecord::contains_word_sequence`, which tokenizes the phrase with the same `engine::normalize_prompt` the caller applied to the prompt and requires a consecutive token run — the same contract as `seed::meanings::surface_present` (issue #386), mirrored for the fact store's own matching path. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1172_factual_qa_subject_match.rs`. |
| R1172-2 | A fact record may answer only when the formalized question's subject (Wikidata Q-id) equals the record's `subject_qid`; alias/keyword matching is retired as the primary mechanism. | Implemented (JavaScript verified locally; the Rust twin is drafted and awaits CI, no local `cargo` run): the subject gate. The question's subject is formalized — the browser worker's `parseFactQuestion` slot, the native `formalize_prompt_candidates` subject anchor when it is already a Wikidata item, otherwise the clause of the prompt that carries the asked `fact_relation` — and resolved to one Q-id through the fact store's own label index (aliases and localized subject labels mapped to `subject_qid`; the longest whole-word label wins, a tie between different Q-ids resolves to nothing). A record with a Q-id answers only when that Q-id and its relation match (`gatedFactRecord` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_factual_qa.js`, `gated_fact_record` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/factual_qa.rs`, which now backs both `try_fact_lookup` and `fact_store_resolves`); R1172-1's word-boundary alias + keyword match survives only as the last-resort `surface_hint` for Q-id-less records (Mona Lisa, Rust creator, …). The admitting gate is logged as `fact_lookup:subject_gate:*`. Pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1172-factual-qa-subject-gate.test.mjs` (R2 cases: "capital of Canada, not the USA" is no longer answered with Washington) and `rust/tests/unit/issue_1172_factual_qa_gate.rs`. The label index is still the seeded fact store, so an entity with no seeded label has no Q-id offline: the live resolution of R1172-3 remains the path for it. |
| R1172-3 | When no seeded fact's subject matches, the engine queries Wikidata live for the requested property and answers from the returned statement with its reference URL. | Implemented (JavaScript verified locally; the Rust side is drafted without a local `cargo` run, CI is its first compile): the native `fact_lookup` row is now a contextual handler (`try_fact_lookup_with_offline` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/fact_live_answer.rs`, dispatched from `rust/src/solver_dispatch.rs`) that answers a seeded record first and otherwise calls `fact_live::resolve_fact_live`. The question is formalized from seed data alone (`live_fact_question`): the relation is the `fact_relation` meaning the prompt names, which must be grounded in a Wikidata property, and the subject term is the relation clause minus the relation's surfaces, the `interrogative_opener` and the `statement_function_word` words (at most four words). The answer renders the new `fact_live_answer` template of `data/seed/multilingual-responses-entities.lino` (en/ru/hi/zh/es) with the claim's reference URL, else the subject snapshot URL, and logs every capture. Transport is enabled only with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_FETCH` and not `offline`; otherwise committed captures replay and a miss falls through. The browser twin `resolveFactQueryViaWikidata` now answers through the same template (`factLiveSummary`, with the seed-cue extractor `factLiveQuestion` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_factual_qa.js`; the browser still routes by `parseFactQuestion`). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1172_live_fact_answer.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1172-live-fact-parity.test.mjs` (fixture transports, no network). |
