## Issue #1173 No Canned Search Answer in the Unknown-Reasoning Fallback

Issue [#1173](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1173) (E138)
deletes the descriptive "Web search requested for `…`" paragraph as an answer
surface and makes the unknown-reasoning fallback execute its web search. The
source analysis, the deleted answer arms, and the evidence live in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1173/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1173-1 | The unknown-reasoning fallback runs the executed search for its focus and answers from the captured statements with citations; offline it answers with the existing `web_search_unavailable` response plus what the offline cache holds. | Implemented: the fallback arm in `rust/src/solver_unknown_reasoning.rs` hands its focus to `answer_web_search_query`, which now executes through `execute_web_search_answer` (`rust/src/solver_handlers/web_requests/live_search.rs`) against the process source cache. Captured sources answer via issue #709 statement fusion with per-statement citations; an offline or cache-miss run still reads the cache and then degrades to the localized `web_search_unavailable` response naming the focus. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1173_fallback_executes_search.rs`. |
| R1173-2 | `answer_web_search_query`'s descriptive text is no longer an answer anywhere; it survives only as narration of the planned search (or is deleted). | Implemented by deletion: every `format!` arm of the old paragraph (default, latest-news, open-research; en and ru) is removed from `rust/src/solver_handlers/web_requests.rs`, and `try_web_search` delegates to the executed path. The provider list and fusion formula survive only as log events (`web_search:provider_planned`, `web_search:fusion_planned`) on the unavailable path — narration in the reasoning trace, never the answer. Pinned by the `no_canned_description` assertions across the same test file. |
| R1173-3 | A request that does not need outside knowledge never reaches the fallback: each class gets its handler through #1175 (routing) and the class issues (#1172, #1174, #1176, #1177, #1178, #1186). | Owned by the #1175 routing work delivered alongside this shard in the same pull request; see its requirement shard. This shard fixes what the fallback does for the prompts that remain. |
| R1173-4 | The answer states what was searched, which pages were read (URL + hash, through #1184's derivation), and which statements the answer rests on. | Implemented for the executed body: the localized fusion header names the query, and every statement lists its source URLs and quotes (issue #709 `render_markdown`). Page-content hashes are #1184's derivation and are not claimed here. Pinned by the citation assertions in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1173_fallback_executes_search.rs`. |
| R1173-5 | Three-roots parity: the browser worker's fallback follows the same rule (translated code, parity case). | Implemented 2026-10-07: the browser worker applies the same rule — `guardCannedWebSearchAnswer` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_reasoning_guards.js`) turns any canned search-machinery description into the seeded `web_search_unavailable` response naming the query, and an offline research prompt never shows it; pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1172-1173-worker-parity.test.mjs`. The TypeScript twin is regenerated from the worker. |

## Issue #1174 Text Transforms Answered Formally

Issue [#1174](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1174) (E139,
part of the #1183 umbrella) gives the solver the text-transform family —
free-text summarization, register rewriting, grammar correction, genre
writing (Conventional Commits and business email), and sentence-level
translation — as computations over text the request itself carries, with all
recognition vocabulary and response prose in seed data and every honest
boundary (nothing to change, slot missing, word unknown) reported through a
seeded template instead of a guess. The probes, the before/after evidence,
and the honest boundaries live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1174/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1174-1 | A summarization request that carries its own paragraph ("Summarize this paragraph: …") is answered with a weight-ranked selection of its statements under a ~30% bound (at least two, always at least one short of the input), never an echo of the source; a request that names no text is declined so the seeded-topic handlers keep it. | Delivered: `handle_summarization_request` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/summarization_request.rs` recognizes the act through the `text_summarization_action` role (surfaces in `data/seed/meanings-summarization.lino`, five languages), extracts the payload with `free_text_payload`, and runs the shared formalize → summarize → deformalize pipeline (`crate::summarization`); statements under two are declined, and the selection bound can never equal the input length. |
| R1174-2 | A register-rewriting request ("Rewrite this formally: can u send me the report asap thx") substitutes every seeded informal token with its formal equivalent (casing kept), splices seeded politeness phrase rules, logs each substitution, and returns a body with no informal token; an already-formal text passes through unchanged with an honest note. | Delivered: `handle_rewrite_register` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/text_rewrite.rs` reads word pairs and phrase rules from `data/seed/register-lexicon.lino` (English and Russian), keeps source casing via `rebuild_core`, and answers through the `text_transform_register` response family; the no-change branch renders `text_transform_rewrite_unchanged`. |
| R1174-3 | A grammar-correction request ("Correct the grammar: She don't like apples and he have two cat.") re-agrees adjacent third-person subject + verb pairs and pluralizes a numeral's noun (irregular plurals and uncountables respected), logging each fix with the rule that fired; a clean text is reported as already grammatical. | Delivered: `handle_grammar_correction` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/text_rewrite.rs` applies the `subject_verb_rule`, `numeral_noun_rule`, `plural_exception` and `uncountable_noun` records of `data/seed/agreement-rules.lino` token by token; corrections render line by line through `text_transform_grammar_line` with the rule name, the body through `text_transform_grammar_result`, and the clean case through `text_transform_grammar_clean`. |
| R1174-4 | A commit-message request ("Write a commit message: correct an off-by-one error in the pagination helper") composes a Conventional Commits line from the described change — verb mapped to the seeded type, scope after the seeded preposition, effect between — and names the genre's missing slots through the incomplete template instead of fabricating them. | Delivered: the `commit_message` arm of `handle_genre_writing` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/text_rewrite.rs` fills the `{type}({component}): {imperative} {effect}` and no-scope templates of `data/seed/writing-genre-styleguides.lino` (styleguide URL logged); a request missing the verb or effect answers through `text_transform_genre_incomplete` at reduced confidence. |
| R1174-5 | An email request ("Write an email to my team: I am taking a day off on Friday because I am tired.") composes the seeded part frames — greeting with recipient, intent, reason after the seeded cue, weekday date, closing — in the styleguide's declared order. | Delivered: the `email` arm of `handle_genre_writing` reads the part sequence, frames, recipient preposition, possessives and reason cue from `data/seed/writing-genre-styleguides.lino`, resolves the weekday through the `calendar_weekday` role, and renders optional parts (reason, date) only when their cues are present. |
| R1174-6 | A translation request whose text has no quotes or backticks ("Translate to Russian: The weather is nice today, let's go for a walk.") still translates: the free sentence after the command head goes word by word through the pipeline, function words are dropped and logged, resolved words carry their meaning ids, unknown words are named through the seeded template rather than hidden, and a sentence with nothing translatable reports the honest gap. | Delivered: `translate_free_sentence` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/mod.rs` (reached from `try_translation` when no quotable surface exists and source ≠ target) calls `TranslationPipeline::translate_sentence` (`rust/src/translation/pipeline.rs`), which resolves each token against seeded compositional lemmas and the cache before any network request, keeps the source token order, and preserves terminal punctuation; unknown words append the `text_transform_translation_unknown` note. |
| R1174-7 | The whole family is a pure function of seed data — cues, pairs, rules, frames, and response prose live in `data/seed/` with five-language response parity — every new token the seed files introduce resolves under the total-closure audit, and no hardcoded-language or literal-predicate debt is added. | Delivered: recognition vocabulary in `register-lexicon.lino`, `agreement-rules.lino`, `writing-genre-styleguides.lino`, `meanings-summarization.lino`; responses in `multilingual-responses-text-transform.lino` (en/ru/hi/zh/es); the new intent keys and identifiers grounded by five-field definitions in `meanings-text-transform.lino` (registered in `data/meta/seed-registry.lino`); all six files measured net-zero unresolved under `scripts/audit-total-closure.py`, and the literal-predicate count stays at its 536 ceiling. |
| R1174-8 | The family is covered by automated tests pinning each probe's intent and computed body, including the honest boundaries (no text to summarize, already formal, already grammatical, missing slots, declined prompts). | Delivered: `rust/tests/unit/issue_1174_text_transform.rs` exercises the handlers directly (the dispatch wiring belongs to the #1175 routing work delivered in the same pull request); its registration in `rust/tests/unit/mod.rs` and the dispatch entries are owned by the coordinating session. |
| R1174-9 | Every answer for these five classes carries its derivation as links (formalized statements, the source-language surface, the target grammar rule or style-guide clause applied) inspectable via `formal-ai explain <answer>`, per the umbrella's white-box requirement (#1183 acceptance item 2). | Implemented 2026-10-07: the handlers log their derivations as evidence-log events (`register_rewrite` per substitution, `grammar_correction` per fix with its rule, `genre_styleguide`/`genre_composition`, `summarization_statement`/`_bound`/`_selected`, and the `translation_*` steps), and the #1184 derivation record now carries them as its `rule` stage: `data/seed/derivation-schema.lino` declares each of those kinds with `collects rule`, `Derivation::record_for` (`rust/src/derivation.rs`) projects every declared kind into an `AppliedRule` (kind + detail), the record round-trips through Links Notation, and `formal-ai explain <answer-id>` prints them under `stage applied_rules` ("not recorded" when a route applied none). A handler joins by naming its event kind in the schema, not by a Rust edit. Pinned by `applied_rules_are_projected_round_tripped_and_explained` and `a_grammar_correction_answer_carries_its_rules_in_the_derivation` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`. The browser worker has no derivation projection yet (R1184-9). |

## Issue #1175 Routing by Formalization, Not by a Surface Word

Issue [#1175](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1175) (E140,
part of the #1183 umbrella) stops two intent detectors from claiming a prompt
because a single word matched a recognition surface: the terminal-command
detector fired whenever a prompt's first word was a seed shell token, and the
software-project detector picked its artifact kind from an artifact surface
anywhere in the prompt. The source analysis, the before/after evidence, and
the honest boundaries live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1175/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1175-1 | The leading-token path of terminal-command detection claims a prompt only when the words after the leading shell token parse as command arguments: no question mark (ASCII or full-width), no colon followed by a space outside quotes, no bare token ending in sentence punctuation (except a token that is entirely dots — `.` and `..` are paths), and no bare function word from a small closed marker list; quoted spans are masked before every check, so prose inside quotes is data. Command shapes stay accepted, including `find . -name '*.log' -size +10M`, `make test`, `head -n 5 main.rs`, `export FOO=bar`, `touch newfile.txt`, `git commit -m 'fix the parser bug'`, and single bare tokens; the backtick+verb and verb+phrase trigger paths are unchanged. | Implemented in `rust/src/solver_terminal.rs` (`parses_as_command_arguments` with `mask_quoted_spans` and `NATURAL_LANGUAGE_MARKER_WORDS`, gated into `leading_shell_command`); JavaScript twin in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_09.js` (`parsesAsCommandArguments` with `maskQuotedSpans`). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing.rs`. |
| R1175-2 | The software-project handler selects its artifact kind only from the head noun of the object phrase governed by the authoring verb — the first boundary-delimited segment after the verb (benefactives and determiners skipped), or, for a verb-final (subject-object-verb) request with nothing after the verb, the last segment before it — never from an artifact word elsewhere in the prompt. Artifact-headed requests keep the frame in every lexicalised language, including unspaced CJK. | Implemented in `rust/src/solver_handlers/software_project.rs` (`object_phrase_artifact` with `skip_object_phrase_lead`, `object_phrase_segments`, `boundary_cut`, `match_artifact_head`, `scan_action_from`; the old any-position `match_artifact`/`scan_match` are deleted; `software_project_claims` and `from_prompt` both route through the new analysis). Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing.rs`. |
| R1175-3 | Routing is decided by a full capability-table refactor so no handler can claim on a surface match alone. | Partial: this change delivers the targeted guards at the two reported detection sites and pins them with held-out probes; the wholesale capability-table refactor of every handler's claims is not delivered here and remains open. Re-checked 2026-10-07: still partial. New routes follow the rule without the table — the #1180 `repository_lineage` route claims only when its cue and an existing repository path are both present — but the shell-command and software-artifact rows of `data/seed/capability-routing.lino`, and the router consulted after formalization before the handler table, do not exist yet. Re-checked 2026-10-07 (fourth pass): the router and the table now exist. The `claim` rows of `data/seed/capability-routing.lino` (registered as a web seed) name a handler, its browser function and the structural evidence kinds that admit it: `software_project` on `object_phrase_artifact` or `approval_of_a_proposal`, `terminal_command` on `shell_command_shape` or `semantic_shell_task`, `repository_lineage` on `repository_subject`. `rust/src/capability_routing/claims.rs` (`claim_admitted`) is consulted by `meta_method_dispatch::try_dispatch` before each handler and by the solver's terminal-command fallback; `claimRouteAdmits` in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_dispatch.js` is the browser twin, consulted before each synchronous handler. A handler with no row is admitted as before. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_claim_routing.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1175-claim-routing.test.mjs`; `rust/tests/web/r1175-routing-probes.test.mjs` and the `js_misroute_ceiling` still hold. Still partial: three handlers carry rows; moving every other handler's claim into a row is what stays open. |
| R1175-4 | A 200-prompt CI routing probe set covers every intent lane with a coverage budget, so a misroute of this class cannot land unnoticed. | Implemented 2026-10-07 for every single-turn lane: 359 held-out probes (256 en, 65 ru, 17 hi, 21 zh; 57 adversarial prose that surface-matches another lane, such as line counts over shell commands and JSON-to-YAML conversions whose keys say `lines`/`count`) in `rust/tests/fixtures/routing-probes/probes-*.lino`, each naming its lane, language and the intent the system should answer. `budget.lino` sets the coverage budget over the 105 shared lanes (every row of `data/seed/handler-precedence.lino`, every slug of `data/seed/intent-routing.lino`, plus the terminal-command detector): 85 lanes carry at least 2 probes; 20 lanes are exempt with a stated reason (10 `browser_only` memory/context rows and 10 follow-up lanes that need an earlier turn), and an exemption for a covered lane fails. The browser worker runs every probe in `rust/tests/web/r1175-routing-probes.test.mjs`; the native solver (offline) in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1175_routing_probes.rs`. Misroutes found while building the corpus are not fixed here: they are ratchets (`js_misroute`, 118 probes, `js_misroute_ceiling 118`; `rust_misroute unverified`, 75 probes the native answer is not yet pinned on, `rust_misroute_ceiling 75`) — a new misroute fails, a fixed browser misroute fails until its line is removed and the ceiling lowered, and the ceilings must equal the listed counts. Boundary: the native test was written without a local cargo run, so its strict set (284 probes) is confirmed by CI, not here. |
| R1175-5 | Three-roots parity: the browser worker's terminal detection and software-project detection follow the same rules. | Implemented 2026-10-07: the terminal-detection guard is mirrored in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_09.js`, and the software-project guard in `detectSoftwareObjectPhrase` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_11.js`, over the shared `objectPhraseArtifact`), so the browser reads the artifact from the request's object phrase as Rust does; `ts/` is regenerated from both. Pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1175-software-object-phrase.test.mjs`. |

## Issue #1176 Quantities, Dates and Statistics Computed Exactly

Issue [#1176](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1176) (E141,
part of the #1183 umbrella) replaces four classes of canned or wrong answers —
calendar offsets, statistics over stated lists, unit conversion, and
price×count word problems — with exact local computation that shows its
arithmetic. The probes, the before/after evidence, and the honest boundaries
live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1176/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1176-1 | Quantities are formalized with value and unit, the unit resolved to a Wikidata item with its conversion factor, and conversions are exact decimal arithmetic; "26.2 miles in km" → 42.1648128 km with the factor 1.609344 cited. | Partial: `rust/src/solver_handlers/unit_conversion.rs` computes conversions on an exact `mantissa × 10⁻ˢᶜᵃˡᵉ` decimal (26.2 × 1.609344 = 42.1648128, 10 km → ≈6.2137119 miles, °C→°F as the formula 25 × 9/5 + 32 = 77) and the answer cites the factor it used. Factors, formulas and unit surfaces are seed data in `data/seed/meanings-units.lino`, each unit grounded in its Wikidata item (mile Q253276, inch Q218593, …) — and the factors are checked against Wikidata itself: `data/cache/unit-conversion/wikidata-P2370.lino` caches each grounded unit's P2370 (conversion to SI unit) statement, fetched 2026-10-07, and `si_factors_match_the_cached_wikidata_conversion_to_si` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1176_quantities_dates.rs` requires every `si_factor` of `data/seed/si-unit-dimensions.lino` to equal it (14 length, mass and time units). The cache is refreshed by hand, not read live at answer time; units are resolved by lexicon surface, not by full item resolution. Unknown units (furlongs) and ambiguous lists ("5 feet 9 inches in cm") are declined. |
| R1176-2 | Word problems are formalized into quantities and relations (price × count, payment − cost) and solved, with the derivation shown (pens: 20 − 4 × 3 = 8). | Implemented: the unit-price pattern (`handle_word_problem` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/statistics.rs`: change 20 − 4 × 3 = 8, total 4 × 3 = 12) is joined by a general relation reading, `statistics/word_relations.rs` (twin `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_word_relations.js`), that folds the stated numbers by the seeded relation words of `data/seed/meanings-statistics.lino` (`word_problem_gain`, `word_problem_loss`, `word_problem_group`, `word_problem_share`, with a `word_problem_question` cue, in en/ru/hi/zh/es): 5 + 3 = 8, 20 - 7 = 13, 6 × 4 = 24, 24 ÷ 6 = 4, 12 + 5 - 4 = 13, and declines numbers no relation word joins. Pinned by `relation_word_problems_derive_from_the_seeded_relation_words` and `relation_word_problems_decline_numbers_no_relation_joins` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1176_quantities_dates.rs` and by `rust/tests/web/issue-1176-word-relations.test.mjs`. Relations beyond these four (rates, comparisons such as "3 more than", multi-step fractions) are not read. |
| R1176-3 | Descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation, percentile, range) are meanings with formulas in `data/seed/meanings-statistics.lino`, applied to the extracted list; mean(4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42) = 18, median = 15.5. | Implemented 2026-10-07: all seven seed-defined operations are delivered in `rust/src/solver_handlers/statistics.rs` and its browser twin `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_statistics.js` — each a meaning with formula and source URL in `data/seed/meanings-statistics.lino`, labels localised from the seed lexemes. Mean 108 / 6 = 18 and median (15 + 16) / 2 = 15.5 are exact; the variance is the exact fraction 5460/36 rendered to seven digits with an explicit ≈ marker (the standard deviation is the one marked approximation). The percentile (`statistics_percentile`) is linear interpolation between closest ranks (the C = 1 variant, Hyndman–Fan definition 7, cited to Wikipedia): the rank stated next to the percentile word ("the 90th percentile", "90-й перцентиль", "percentil 90", "第90百分位数") leaves the dataset as a parameter, and the answer is exact with its derivation from the seed template `statistics_percentile_derivation` in five languages — 90th percentile of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5: rank = 1 + (5 - 1) × 90 / 100 = 4.6; 4 + 0.6 × (5 - 4) = 4.6. A missing or out-of-range rank is declined. |
| R1176-4 | Calendar arithmetic reads the formalized offset (quantity and unit: days, weeks, months) and computes modulo the cycle: 100 days after Monday = 14 weeks + 2 days → Wednesday. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `try_calendar_reasoning` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/calendar.rs` (twin: `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_calendar_offset.js`) reads the stated offset — numeral plus unit surface from the seed (`calendar_day`, `calendar_week`, `calendar_month`), spelled cardinals included, CJK-unspaced "100天" and "2个月" included — and shifts by it: 100 days after Monday is Wednesday with the derivation "100 days = 14 weeks + 2 days"; whole weeks state that the weekday is unchanged. Month offsets (`rust/src/solver_handlers/calendar/month.rs`): from a month name (the twelve `calendar_month_name` meanings, Wikidata Q108–Q126) they are exact modulo-12 arithmetic with the derivation shown — 5 months after November: 11 + 5 = 16 ≡ 4 (mod 12), April; from a weekday they have no single answer, because a month is no fixed number of days, so the answer is a clarification that names why and shows the day span the months can cover over a full 400-year Gregorian cycle (3 months span 89 to 92 days) and asks for the starting date. A bare "the day after X" keeps its original ±1 reading. Real-calendar date arithmetic (a dated start plus months, end-of-month clamping) is not part of this row. |
| R1176-5 | Each answer carries its derivation and all three roots answer identically. | Implemented 2026-10-07: every answer body shows the arithmetic it performed (derivation strings in `data/seed/multilingual-responses-quantities.lino`, 12 intents × 5 languages), the evidence log carries `calendar:offset`, `statistics:<op>`, `unit_conversion:<step>`, `word_problem:<role>` events, and #1184's derivation record (`derivation::finalize_answer`) completes every route. The browser worker and the TypeScript twin answer the same probes (R1176-6). |
| R1176-6 | Worker parity: the unit-conversion, statistics, word-problem and calendar-offset computations answer identically in the browser worker and the TypeScript root (pull-request follow-up row: the three-roots half of R1176-5). | Implemented 2026-10-07: unit conversion, statistics, word problems and calendar offsets have browser-worker twins that reproduce the Rust handlers' exact-decimal arithmetic and derivation text, and `ts/` is regenerated from them; pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1176-unit-conversion-parity.test.mjs`, `issue-1176-statistics-parity.test.mjs` and `issue-1176-calendar-offset-parity.test.mjs`. |

## Issue #1177 Code Tasks Answered Formally

Issue [#1177](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1177) (E142,
part of the #1183 umbrella) gives the solver nine code-task families —
debugging, regular-expression synthesis, SQL synthesis, shell-command
composition, code explanation, code review, test generation, code
refactoring, and JSON/YAML format conversion — as structural derivations
from seed vocabulary, with every answer stating honestly that no code,
query, command, regex or generated test was executed. The probes, the
before/after evidence, and the honest boundaries live in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1177/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1177-1 | A "find the bug / debug this" request over a function is answered by deriving the defect structurally — a binary `+`/`-` applied at top level after a division shifts the quotient and contradicts what the function name promises — with the line quoted, both fixes shown (reorder, parenthesize), and the property grounded in a source. | Partial: `handle_code_debugging` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/code_debugging.rs` reads `def`/`fn`/`function` lines, resolves the name's promised property against the `function_intent` records in `data/seed/meanings-code-structure-explanations.lino` (each with a math source URL), and flags `sum(xs) / len(xs) - 1` as mean-minus-one with both candidate fixes; inline one-line returns are scanned too. A second defect class needs no function name: a loop bound from the seeded `index_bound_past_end` table in `data/seed/code-task-cues.lino` (`range(len(xs) + 1)`, `<= len(xs)`, `<= arr.length`, `<= v.size()`, `<= v.len()`) is reported only when the same code indexes that collection, with the bound that stops one position earlier (`handler_code_debugging_reports_a_loop_bound_past_the_end`; JS twin in `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_code_tasks.js`, pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-code-tasks-parity.test.mjs`). A third class is an assignment inside a parenthesized condition that opens with a head from the seeded `assignment_in_condition` table (`if (`, `while (`). It needs a lone `=` at the condition's top level, outside quoted text, so a deliberate nested `while ((line = read()) != null)` is not reported. The fix is the comparison (`handler_code_debugging_reports_an_assignment_inside_a_condition` and its browser twin). Other defect classes fall to the honest no-defect template, which names all three covered classes. No code is executed and the answer says so. |
| R1177-2 | A regular-expression request ("five digits optionally followed by a hyphen and four digits") is composed from count, class, separator, optionality and anchor vocabulary, verified structurally, and never run against a string. | Partial: `handle_regex_synthesis` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/regex_synthesis.rs` composes from the seed word maps in `data/seed/code-task-cues.lino` (number words, classes, separators, optional markers, anchor exceptions) into anchored patterns — `^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$`, `\d{3,}` for "three or more" — and `verify_structurally` rejects dangling escapes and unbalanced repetition/parens/classes before answering. Unresolvable requests are refused by name. No match is executed and the answer says so. |
| R1177-3 | A SQL request ("select all users older than 30") is composed into a SELECT with table, columns, WHERE filters, aggregate, ORDER BY and LIMIT — each clause mapped back to the request words that produced it — and nothing is executed against a database. | Partial: `handle_sql_synthesis` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/sql_synthesis.rs` composes the statement from seed comparatives ("older than N" → `age > N`), generic column comparisons, named filters, aggregates, "sorted by X" and "top N" cues; the answer carries a request→emission mapping row per clause and states the verification is by construction. An aggregate is grouped by the column a seeded grouping cue names (`sql_grouping` in `data/seed/code-task-cues.lino`: "per country", "for each department", "grouped by city", "для каждого …") — `SELECT country, COUNT(*) FROM users GROUP BY country;` with its own mapping row — and the browser twin composes the same statement (`handler_sql_synthesis_groups_an_aggregate_by_the_seeded_cue`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-code-synthesis-parity.test.mjs`). A threshold stated after the grouping becomes HAVING on the aggregate: a seeded `sql_having` cue ("having", "with", "имеющих") followed by a seeded `sql_threshold` comparator ("more than", "at least", "меньше", …) gives `SELECT customer, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY customer HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;`. That span is no longer read as a WHERE filter, which before this fix emitted `WHERE with > 5`. A comparison stated before the grouping stays in WHERE (`handler_sql_synthesis_filters_groups_with_having_after_the_grouping` and its browser twin). A join is read from the seeded `sql_join` roles: the joined table is the first non-filler word after a `join` word, and the shared column the first non-filler word after a `key` word ("joined with the orders table on user_id", "соедини с таблицей orders по user_id"). It is emitted as `JOIN orders USING (user_id)`, and without a stated key no join is guessed (`handler_sql_synthesis_joins_on_a_stated_shared_column` and its browser twin). Both runtimes tokenize the lowercased prompt with edge punctuation trimmed, so `user_id` keeps its underscore whichever normalization the caller applied. Still single SELECT statements: no subqueries and no join on differently named columns. Identifying neither table nor cue refuses by name. |
| R1177-4 | A file-finding request ("find .log files larger than 10 MB under /var") is composed into a shell command with a cited manual page, and not executed. | Partial: `handle_shell_command_compose` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/shell_command_compose.rs` composes `find` with `-name` and `-size` clauses from the seed `file_context` and `size_unit` maps (MB/MiB → `M`, KB/KiB → `k`), cites the findutils manual, and marks the command Not executed. Beyond `find`, the same composer (twin `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_shell_compose.js`) reads four more verb families from seed cues, each flag explained from its manual page: line slices (`head`/`tail -n`, "show the last 20 lines of app.log"), content search (`grep -r`, with `-i` for an ignore-case cue and a Russian containment cue), directory listings (`ls`), and a seeded counting cue that pipes the result into `wc -l`. Pinned by `handler_shell_compose_slices_lines_and_searches_content` and the counting and Russian-grep tests in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_code_task_handlers.rs`, and by `rust/tests/web/issue-1177-shell-compose-parity.test.mjs`. A substitution request ("replace 1.0 with 2.0 in version.txt", "замени foo на bar в файле config.txt") composes `sed -i 's/1\.0/2.0/g' version.txt`. It reads seeded `substitute` / `substitute_with` role words, escapes the pattern and the replacement so they match literally, and refuses a word that holds the delimiter or a quote. Both flags are explained from the GNU sed manual record (`handler_shell_compose_composes_a_literal_sed_substitution` and its browser twin). A substitution with no file argument is not claimed. Verbs outside these families (awk, xargs pipelines, archive tools, sed scripts beyond one literal substitution) are refused by name rather than guessed. |
| R1177-5 | An "explain this code" request is answered line by line: each line matched against a construct table with a grounding URL, placeholders filled from the actual code, and an overall summary of what the function name promises. | Partial: `handle_code_explanation` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/code_explanation.rs` matches constructs (def, return, division, loops, builtins, conditionals, promise chains) from `data/seed/meanings-code-structure-explanations.lino`, each with sentence template and source, and closes with the name-promise summary. Unknown lines are skipped, not guessed; no code is executed and the answer says so. |
| R1177-6 | A "review this code" request reports only rule findings the code actually matches, each with severity, the quoted line, advice, and an upstream source URL — and no lint tool is run. | Partial: `handle_code_review` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/code_review.rs` applies the five seed rules in `data/seed/code-review-rules.lino` — bare `except:`, mutable default argument, `== None` instead of `is None`, `+=` string building in a loop (Python), loose `==` coercion (JavaScript) — each citing docs.python.org, PEP 8 or MDN. Language is detected from markers; a clean review says no match was found. No linter is executed and the answer says so. |
| R1177-7 | A "write tests for `f(x)`" request emits a runnable-looking pytest suite for a recognized problem shape, with expected values the shape's table states — and the suite is never executed. | Partial: `handle_test_generation` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/test_generation.rs` matches the function under test to the seed `test_cases` shapes (palindrome, average, max; trigger words are seed data), emits parametrized cases from the stated expectations (`RaceCar` → true, `never odd or even` → true, `[2, 4, 6]` → 4), and adds a `normalize()` helper when case-insensitivity/space/punctuation cues are present. Unknown shapes get a smoke skeleton and the derivation says the shape was not recognized. NOT executed, and the answer says so. |
| R1177-8 | A refactoring request performs the one implemented structural transformation — a JavaScript promise chain becomes an `async function` with `await`, handler bodies preserved verbatim — and refuses anything else by name. | Partial: `handle_code_refactoring` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/code_refactoring.rs` parses `.then`/`.catch` chains (arrow and `function` handlers), renders each `.then` as `const <param> = await <previous>;` in order with the catch clause preserved, and states the equivalence check is structural. Promise chains are the one transformation; other refactoring targets are refused by name. No code is executed and the answer says so. |
| R1177-9 | A JSON↔YAML conversion request converts the document, round-trips the result through the same subset parser, and compares against the input value; anything outside the subset is refused with a named reason. | Partial: `handle_format_conversion` in `rust/src/solver_handlers/format_conversion.rs` renders a JSON `Value` to block-style YAML and parses YAML back with a subset parser (mappings, sequences, scalars); the round-trip value equality check gates the answer, and bad JSON, a failed round trip or non-subset YAML each refuse through their own seed reason template. The subset excludes anchors, multi-line literals and flow style. No file or network I/O. |
| R1177-10 | All nine families are pure functions of seed data — cues, word maps, rule tables and answer prose live in `data/seed/` — refuse unrelated prompts, and are covered by automated tests at handler and engine level. | Implemented: recognition cues and word maps are in `data/seed/code-task-cues.lino`, review rules in `data/seed/code-review-rules.lino`, response templates in `data/seed/multilingual-responses.lino`, and every new intent key, scope, role and package token is defined in `data/seed/meanings-code-task-templates.lino`. `rust/tests/unit/issue_1177_code_task_handlers.rs` pins all nine probes at handler and engine level (the dispatch rows are wired in `rust/src/solver_dispatch.rs`), plus the refusal of unrelated prompts. All nine have browser-worker twins (`rust/tests/web/issue-1177-code-tasks-parity.test.mjs`, `issue-1177-code-synthesis-parity.test.mjs`, `issue-1177-format-conversion-parity.test.mjs`, `issue-1177-shell-compose-parity.test.mjs`), and `ts/` is regenerated from them. |
| R1177-11 | None of the nine sub-classes' answers ever recite a fetched Rosetta Code example verbatim (`rust/src/coding/rosetta_request.rs`'s `render_example` path is for the "example" intent only, not for explanation/debugging/review/etc.); the no-memorization gate (`rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/no_memorization.rs`) is extended to scan the new handlers' output surfaces the same way it scans `coding-discovery-runtime.lino`. | Implemented: the no-memorization gate now scans the nine handlers' output surfaces (`CODE_TASK_OUTPUT_SURFACES` — the code-task response templates, explanation meanings, review rules, manual pages and recognition cues) with the same whole-algorithm rule it applies to `coding-discovery-runtime.lino`, generalized from `text` values to every quoted value (`code_task_output_surfaces_carry_no_whole_algorithm`), and pins that none of the nine handler sources reaches `rosetta_request` / `render_example` (`code_task_handlers_never_recite_rosetta_examples`), both in `rust/tests/unit/coding_discovery/no_memorization.rs`. |
| R1177-12 | HumanEval and MBPP are re-measured on their full upstream slices after the change and the resulting pass counts are recorded, whatever they are, in `data/benchmarks/external-results.lino` (consumed by `docs/status.md`'s "Latest external benchmark rows" table). | Open, blocked on a hang: the full-slice HumanEval dispatch (`external-benchmarks.yml`, suite `humaneval`, slice 164, run 37578344303 on `28443684c`) printed nothing after the dataset download and was cancelled at the 90-minute job cap, so no pass count exists to record. The runner now prints every case before and after it is solved, and the dataset download has connect and transfer timeouts, so the next dispatch names the case that stalls. `data/benchmarks/external-results.lino` still carries the pre-change rows. HumanEval and then MBPP are re-dispatched after this push. |

## Issue #1180 Repository History as Formal Context

Issue [#1180](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1180) (E145,
part of the E127 umbrella #1183) asks for the repository's full history —
commits, issues, pull requests, comments, reviews and Actions runs — to be
formalized into records the solver can query, so lineage questions ("which
issue asked for X and which pull request delivered it") have an answer.
R1180-1 through R1180-8 are the issue's own numbered requirements; R1180-9
through R1180-11 are derived from its "What to build", "How to test" and
"Depends on" sections so that nothing the issue asks for goes untracked. The
timeline, root causes and verification live in
`docs/case-studies/issue-1180/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1180-1 | A commit importer walks `git log` on the working repository and formalizes each commit's author, committer date, subject, body, trailers (`Refs #NNN`, `Closes #NNN`, `Co-Authored-By:`) and changed paths into one record per commit. | Implemented: `rust/src/history_context/commits.rs` (`import_commits`, `formalize_commit`) records author role, committer date, subject plus body as content, every changed path as `path:` evidence, the `Refs`/`Closes` trailers as `issue:` evidence and the conversation id, and every `Co-Authored-By:` trailer (the seed's `coauthor_trailer` row in `data/seed/history-formalization.lino`, read by `coauthors` in `rust/src/history_context/items.rs`) as `coauthor:<name>` evidence. Pinned by `commit_formalization_extracts_trailers_and_changed_symbols` and `coauthor_trailers_become_evidence` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`. The seed rows were silently ignored before this change because `HistoryRules::from_seed_text` did not descend under the `history_formalization` root; `rules_seed_rows_override_the_defaults` pins the fix. The importer passes its record format as `--format=` since 46d45c9e1. |
| R1180-2 | For every changed `.rs` path the importer runs `self_ast::ast_census` on the pre- and post-image blobs (`es_meta` for `.js`/`.ts`) and records which top-level items differ, not only which paths changed. | Implemented: `diff_symbols` reads both blobs with `git show` and, besides the census histogram delta, records each named top-level item that was added (+1), removed (-1) or modified (0) as `symbol:<path>#<keyword> <name>` evidence (`diff_named_items` in `rust/src/history_context/items.rs`). The item keywords (`fn struct enum trait ...` for Rust, `function class const ...` for JS/TS), the span keyword `impl` and the modifiers (`pub async export ...`) are seed rows. Pinned by `changed_items_are_recorded_by_name` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`. The names come from a line-level scan of the seed's keywords, not from the AST: an item opened inside a macro or on an indented line is not named. |
| R1180-3 | An issue/PR importer reuses `github_logs`'s capture and formalizes title, body, labels, state transitions and issue↔PR/commit links. | Implemented 2026-10-07: besides title plus body, labels, the current state and the `Refs`/`Closes`/merge links, `formalize_issue_or_pull` (`rust/src/history_context/github.rs`) now records each body line that opens with the seed's requirement marker and a number as `requirement:R<n> <statement>` evidence (`requirement_statements`, `rust/src/history_context/statements.rs`; a prose reference such as `R1180-3` is not a statement), and the capture's `createdAt`/`closedAt`/`mergedAt` stamps as dated `state:<state>@<timestamp>` transitions in chronological order (`state_transitions`). The states, their timestamp fields, the marker, its leads and the evidence prefixes are the `state_transition`, `state_evidence` and `requirement_statement` rows of `data/seed/history-formalization.lino`; `formal-ai github-logs` now captures `closedAt` (issues) and `closedAt,mergedAt` (pull requests) so the transitions are dated. Pinned by `issue_bodies_formalize_into_requirement_statements_and_dated_transitions` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs` and its JS twin in `rust/tests/web/issue-1180-history-statements-lineage.test.mjs`. Boundary: transitions are those the capture dates (opened, closed, merged); a reopen-then-close cycle shows only the last close, because the capture has no timeline API. |
| R1180-4 | A comments/reviews importer formalizes each comment and review as one record with author, body and timestamp, linked to its parent issue or PR. | Implemented: comment and review batches in `rust/src/history_context/github.rs` become `review` events whose conversation id is `issue-N`/`pr-N` and whose evidence names the parent; covered by `issue_and_pr_import_links_commit_to_source_issue` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`. |
| R1180-5 | A CI-run importer formalizes each Actions run (`databaseId`, `workflowName`, `conclusion`, `headSha`, `jobs`) into one record per run, carrying the failing step and error text when the run failed. | Implemented: `import_ci_runs` with `failing_step_lines` in `rust/src/history_context/github.rs`, pinned by `ci_run_import_carries_failing_steps` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`. |
| R1180-6 | Every importer is incremental from a stored cursor, and two back-to-back runs with no new history add zero records. | Implemented: `RepositoryHistoryCursor`, `import_incremental` and the id-deduplicating `write_repository_history` in `rust/src/history_context/cursor.rs`, pinned by `incremental_import_is_idempotent` and `incremental_import_only_advances_past_the_watermark` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`. |
| R1180-7 | All five record kinds are `MemoryEvent` values with `kind` in `commit / issue / pull_request / review / ci_run`, queryable through the existing memory query language with no schema change. | Implemented: the kind spellings and id prefixes are seed rows in `data/seed/history-formalization.lino`; the lineage `SELECT id FROM memory WHERE kind = 'pull_request' AND evidence LIKE '%issue:1014%'` runs through the unchanged `compile_memory_query`/`execute_memory_query` in `issue_and_pr_import_links_commit_to_source_issue` (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`). |
| R1180-8 | The lineage query for `scripts/check-self-development-release.rs` returns exactly the six commits `git log --follow` lists, each with its issue and pull request. | Implemented with one caveat: `on_this_repo_check_self_development_release_lineage` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs` asserts all six commits (`88d368a5b`, `02f590106`, `96f405e0d`, `aa6a5d085`, `9efeb735c`, `33451d012`), chronological order, and `issue-1014`/`pr:1015` on the introducing commit. The issue and pull request of the five later commits are not asserted, and the test returns early on a shallow clone. |
| R1180-9 | A `formal-ai repository-history import / query` subcommand exposes the importer, following the `cli_github_logs` pattern. | Implemented: `formal-ai repository-history import` and `formal-ai repository-history query <SQL>` (`rust/src/cli_repository_history.rs`, wired in `rust/src/main.rs`) run `import_incremental` and the read-only `query_repository_history` (`rust/src/history_context/query.rs`, ANSI SQL through the unchanged memory query language). The library half is pinned by `the_repository_history_store_answers_a_query` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`; the argument parsing itself has no test. |
| R1180-10 | `formal-ai chat` answers "why does the self-development status fail?" (and the #1180 probe "what does `evaluate_calculation` do?") from the threshold, the commit range and the rule's source issue. | Implemented 2026-10-07 (this pull request, fourth pass; the engine-level answers are verified by CI, no local cargo run): the status and definition questions are now answered. Earlier the same day: the `repository_lineage` solver route (`handle_repository_lineage` in `rust/src/history_context/lineage.rs`, rank 162 in `data/seed/handler-precedence.lino`, before formalization and search) answers a lineage question about a repository path from that path's `git log --follow` history: the commits oldest first, the issue the introducing commit was made for (its trailer) and the pull request whose merge delivered it, each read through the seed's own trailer and merge patterns; an unrecorded one is said to be unrecorded. It claims only when a seeded `lineage_cue` phrase (en/ru/hi/zh/es, `data/seed/history-formalization.lino`) and a path that exists in the working repository are both present, so a cue word alone never claims (#1175). The prose is the `repository_lineage` records of `data/seed/multilingual-responses-formalization.lino` in five languages. Pinned by `lineage_subjects_need_a_cue_and_a_path`, `lineage_answer_names_the_commits_issue_and_unrecorded_pull_request` and `chat_answers_a_lineage_question_from_this_repositorys_history` (skipped on a shallow clone) in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_history_context.rs`; JS twin `js/agentic/crate/history_lineage.mjs`, pinned by `rust/tests/web/issue-1180-history-statements-lineage.test.mjs`. Still open: "why does the self-development status fail?" needs the threshold and commit range explained, not only the lineage, and "what does `evaluate_calculation` do?" needs a definition lookup (the `repository_qa` class); symbol lineage (`git log -S`) is not routed. The browser worker has no repository, so the route is native-only (an `exempt_lane` in the routing-probe budget). Fourth pass: when no lineage subject is present the route hands the prompt to `rust/src/history_context/repository_qa.rs`. A seeded `status_cue` ("self-development status" and its ru/hi/zh/es forms) is answered from the `status_rule` of `data/seed/history-formalization.lino`: the commit range from the newest `v[0-9]*` tag to HEAD (`git describe`, `git rev-list --count`) and how many of its commits carry the `Formal-AI-Session` trailer, the floor, unit and attribution and the newest release target (basis points to percent) read from `data/meta/self-hosting-ledger.lino`, and the issue that introduced `scripts/check-self-development-release.rs` (its `git log --follow` trailer, #1014); the answer says it reads the range and the ledger and does not run the measurement. A seeded `definition_cue` ("what does", "что делает", "做什么", "qué hace" …) with an identifier-shaped token the self-AST census (`data/meta/self-ast/src`) records is answered with the symbol's kind, file and line span, the first paragraph of its `///` documentation comment read from the source, and the commit that introduced it (`git log -S` over the file's extension) with that commit's issue; at most three symbols. Prose is the `repository_status_explanation` and `repository_definition*` records in five languages. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1180_repository_qa.rs` (including engine-level answers through `FormalAiEngine`) and the JS twin `js/agentic/crate/history_repository_qa.mjs` by `rust/tests/web/issue-1180-repository-qa.test.mjs`. The `repository_lineage` claim row of `data/seed/capability-routing.lino` (R1175-3) admits the route on a path, status or census-symbol subject. |

## Issue #1181 Standalone CLI Binaries and Consistent Boolean Env Switches

Issue [#1181](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1181) (E146,
part of the #1183 umbrella) has two halves: people cannot *run* the released
CLI at all (the release ships desktop apps and a VSIX but no standalone
`formal-ai` binary — the only channels are a full `cargo install` source build
or a 24.3 GB container image, #1153), and the one env switch that gates CLI
output rejects the conventional `1`/`0` spellings (`FORMAL_AI_SILENT=1
formal-ai chat …` fails with `invalid value '1' for '--silent' [possible
values: true, false]`). The evidence, the design, and the per-file change list
live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1181/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1181-1 | `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml` gains a `cli` job that builds `formal-ai` for `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and uploads one archive per target to the same GitHub Release the `build`/`vscode` jobs publish to. | Delivered as workflow: the `cli` job in `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml` (five-leg matrix mirroring the `build` job's needs/concurrency/if/permissions/checkout/sccache conventions, `taiki-e/setup-cross-toolchain-action@v1` for the musl legs because the dependency graph compiles C code). Observable on the next tagged release, whose asset list must show the five `formal-ai-cli-*` archives; until then it is code-reviewed, not executed. |
| R1181-2 | Each archive is named `formal-ai-cli-<target-triple>.tar.gz` (`.zip` for the Windows target), contains the `formal-ai` binary plus `LICENSE` and `README.md` under a top-level `formal-ai-cli-<triple>/` directory, and is reproducible from `cargo build --release --target <triple> --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --bin formal-ai --locked`. | Delivered as workflow: the "Package the CLI archive" and "Smoke test CLI archive" steps build with the exact pinned-lock command, package the staging directory, then extract the archive on the leg's own runner and run `./formal-ai --version` plus non-emptiness checks on `LICENSE`/`README.md`. |
| R1181-3 | The `finalize` job's consolidated `SHA256SUMS.txt` and `BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt` cover the five CLI archives alongside the existing desktop/VSIX assets, in the same files, with the same "INCOMPLETE" honesty reporting for partial matrices. | Delivered as workflow: `cli` joins `finalize`'s `needs`; each leg uploads a `SHA256SUMS-cli-<label>.partial` fragment (the `cli-` label prefix prevents collision with the desktop legs' identically-shaped labels in the merged `fragments/` directory); the `builder_of` map and label loop in `finalize` gain the five `cli-*` labels mapped to their runners. |
| R1181-4 | `rust/Cargo.toml` gains a `[package.metadata.binstall]` table so `cargo binstall formal-ai` resolves one of the R2 archives without a source build. | Delivered: `[package.metadata.binstall]` (`pkg-url` …/`formal-ai-cli-{ target }.tar.gz`, `pkg-fmt "tgz"`, `bin-dir "formal-ai-cli-{ target }/{ bin }{ binary-ext }"`) with a `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` override to the `.zip`; the URL is written out literally because the archive name ends `.tar.gz`, not binstall's default `{ archive-suffix }` (`.tgz`). Executed only when the first release carrying the assets exists. |
| R1181-5 | `scripts/install.sh`'s `install_cli()` and `install.ps1`'s equivalent download and verify the matching `formal-ai-cli-<target>` archive first, falling back to `cargo install formal-ai` only when no matching archive exists for the host's OS/arch (e.g. windows-arm64, which R1 does not build). | Delivered: `install_cli_prebuilt`/`Install-CliPrebuilt` resolve the host triple, fetch the archive, verify it against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt` through the existing `verify_checksum`/`Test-Checksum` helpers, run the installed binary's `--version`, and only then report success; any unavailable/failed prebuilt path falls back to the unchanged `cargo install` body. A checksum mismatch still aborts (it never falls back silently). `install.ps1` could not be machine-parsed on this macOS workstation (no PowerShell); it follows the file's existing cmdlet idioms and is review-verified. |
| R1181-6 | A single boolean-env parser accepts `1/0/true/false/yes/no/on/off` case-insensitively (surrounding whitespace tolerated; anything else is unrecognised, never silently coerced), is the `value_parser` for every clap arg with `env = "FORMAL_AI_*"` on a `bool` field, and is used by every ad-hoc `std::env::var("FORMAL_AI_*")` boolean read in `rust/src`. | Delivered and tested: `rust/src/cli_env.rs` (`parse_bool_env`, `bool_env_value_parser`, `flag_enabled`, `flag_disabled`) wired into `rust/src/main.rs`'s `--silent` (the only clap bool arg with an `env` attribute in the crate) and into every ad-hoc boolean read — the full converted-site list is in `docs/case-studies/issue-1181/README.md`. `solver_helpers::env_bool`/`env_bool_with_extra_truthy` now delegate to the same table so there is one spelling vocabulary crate-wide. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1181_boolean_env_parser.rs`. The one intentional exception: `FORMAL_AI_FULL_TRUST` (`rust/src/bounded_autonomy.rs`) keeps its exact-`"1"` sentinel because it is a security opt-in, not a UX switch. `rust/src/translation/pipeline.rs`'s `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG` read is deferred to the issue-#1174 change that owns that file. |
| R1181-7 | `FORMAL_AI_SILENT=1 formal-ai chat --prompt …` (and `=true`, `=yes`, `=on`, case-insensitive, and their false-y counterparts) no longer errors, and the non-clap `verbose_enabled()` read of the same variable honours the same spellings. | Delivered and tested: the `value_parser = formal_ai::cli_env::bool_env_value_parser` attribute on `--silent` (the `SetTrue` action is preserved, so a bare `--silent` flag still works), and `dialog_log::verbose_enabled()`'s second read goes through `!flag_enabled("FORMAL_AI_SILENT")`. Pinned by `silent_switch_now_accepts_one_as_the_issue_reported` and `bool_env_value_parser_maps_spellings_to_clap_results` in the same test file, which assert the exact truth table for the reported failing value. |

| Requirement | Status | Evidence / remaining work |
|---|---|---|
| R8 In-repo duplicate-function gate | Drafted library script | Corrected lexical scanner, SHA-256 grouping, explicit baseline initialization, fresh/stale checks; fixture tests drafted. No runtime verification. |

| Weekly workflow | Drafted scan-only default | Resolves credential, installs toolchain/runner, scans and uploads record. Opening issues requires explicit workflow input; no issues opened during implementation. |

Named-function scanning is lexical, not AST based. Rust/JavaScript closures, methods without keywords, regex literals and template interpolation need meta-language grammar integration. No Rust builds, tests, package commands or issue creation were run locally.

## Issue #1184 White-Box Derivation for Every Answer

Issue [#1184](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1184) (E148)
requires the meta algorithm to be white box: every answer carries its
derivation — search queries, fetched URLs with hashes, formalized fragments,
decomposed parts, the recomposition, the rendering, the verification — as a
durable record keyed by a content-addressed `derivation_id`, and
`formal-ai explain <answer-id>` prints it afterwards. The audit of what
`EventLog`, `SourceCapture`, and `VerifiedAnswer` already provide, the plan,
and the delivery survey live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1184/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1184-1 | Every `SymbolicAnswer` the solver returns carries a `derivation_id`, content-addressed the way `VerifiedAnswer::derivation_id` is, surfaced on every calling surface. | Implemented: `SymbolicAnswer::derivation_id` computes `stable_id("answer", &answer)` from the current answer text, and its custom `Serialize` includes the id in every JSON response; `UniversalSolver` finalizes all of its return paths with a derivation link. Since 2026-10-07 every calling surface carries it: the browser worker's `finalize` result has `derivationId` (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker_20.js`, read by `js/app/app-conversation-hooks.jsx`), and the `/v1/responses` object of both servers has `derivation_id` (R1184-8). Pinned by `every_symbolic_answer_carries_a_stable_derivation_id`, `solver_early_returns_expose_serialized_id_and_live_record` and `the_derivation_id_is_the_same_constant_in_every_root` (`answer_91f06b150735a87e`) in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs`, and by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-id-surfaces.test.mjs` for the worker and the JS server. |
| R1184-2 | A `Derivation` record per answer captures search queries, fetches with SHA-256 and timestamps, formalized fragments, decomposed parts, recomposition, rendering, and verification evidence. | Implemented: `Derivation::record_for(log, answer_id)` projects `EventLog::events()` — `web_search:request` and both `source:http` payload spellings today; `formalize:fragment`, `decompose:part`, `recompose:bind`, `render:emit`, `verify:evidence` are named public constants the E128/E129/E131/E132 landings append. Pinned by `derivation_carries_search_queries_fetches_and_hashes_for_an_online_answer`. |
| R1184-3 | The record is durable and queryable after the answer is returned, keyed by `derivation_id`, without replaying the request. | Implemented: `Derivation::persist`/`load` under `data/cache/derivations/<answer_id>.lino` (the `sources-registry` `cache_path` convention), lossless lino round-trip and honest miss pinned by `durable_record_round_trips_by_answer_id`; path-traversing ids are refused. |
| R1184-4 | `formal-ai explain <answer-id>` prints the full derivation from the durable store. | Implemented: the `Explain` subcommand in `rust/src/main.rs` backed by `rust/src/cli_explain.rs` (`--format text` readable, `--format links` the canonical record); the shared miss message names the id shape and the store path. |
| R1184-5 | A stage the route never populated reports "not recorded" — never fabricated or inferred. | Implemented: `explain_text` names every stage and prints `not recorded`; the lino record omits absent stages entirely. Pinned by `explain_reports_not_recorded_for_stages_a_route_did_not_populate`. |
| R1184-6 | The `--thinking` trace and the derivation record are two projections of the same `EventLog`. | Implemented: `record_for` reads `EventLog::events()` and nothing else — the same log `thinking_steps_for_answer` curates. Pinned by `explain_and_thinking_trace_agree_on_the_same_event_log` (the narrated `http_chat` details are exactly the derivation's queries; the derivation additionally keeps fetch hashes the thinking view intentionally drops). |
| R1184-7 | `formal-ai explain` and the self-explanation recipe (`agentic_coding/explain.rs`) keep disjoint triggers. | Implemented and pinned: the subcommand takes a content-addressed id argument and never inspects the running codebase; `explain_command_does_not_collide_with_the_self_explanation_recipe` asserts the recipe's keywords are untouched and an answer id is not one of them. |
| R1184-8 | The Serve API's JSON response includes `derivation_id` alongside `evidence_links`. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `ResponseObject` (`rust/src/protocol/output.rs`) gains `derivation_id`, set by `response_from_symbolic` (`rust/src/protocol.rs`) to the id of the answer the response renders and placed beside `evidence_links` (which already names `derivation:<id>`); a planned tool-call response carries no solver answer and omits it. The JavaScript server's `responseFromSymbolic` (`js/server/responses.mjs`) emits the same field in the same position. Pinned by `the_responses_api_carries_the_derivation_id_beside_evidence_links` in `rust/tests/unit/issue_1184_derivation_records.rs` and by `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-id-surfaces.test.mjs`. |
| R1184-9 | Three-roots parity: `derivation` module translated to js/ts roots with cross-runtime derivation cases. | Partially delivered. JS root: `js/agentic/crate/derivation.mjs` mirrors every pub item of `rust/src/derivation.rs` (record projection over `{kind, payload}` events in append order, both `source:http` spellings, `VerificationRecord` payload/parse, `to_lino`/`from_lino`, `explain_text`, `answer_derivation_id`, `store_path`, `miss_message`, applied rules read from the schema's `stage ... collects rule` rows of `data/seed/derivation-schema.lino`). Since 2026-10-07 `persist`, `load` and `explainAnswer` mirror `Derivation::persist`/`load` and `explain_answer` over an injected `{ readText, writeText, createDirAll }` io (the host offers no write, the convention `discovery_production.mjs` uses for the procedure cache): the file at `storePath` holds the `toLino` bytes, a record filed under another id or an unusable id is a miss, and the miss is the seed's `derivation_record_missing` text; `durable record round-trips by answer id` in the parity test pins the exact path, bytes and miss text over `node:fs`. `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-parity.test.mjs` replays the Rust unit cases and pins byte-identical `to_lino` text. TS root: since 2026-10-07 `scripts/translate-es.mjs` renders it as `ts/agentic/crate/derivation.mts`. Cross-runtime case (2026-10-07): `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` gains `e1184_derivation_answer_id`, a prompt both solvers answer byte for byte (`DERIVATION ANSWER EVERY`); its `expectedDerivationEvidence` field is the exact `derivation:<answer id>` link, which `rust/tests/unit/specification/synthesis.rs` asserts on the Rust answer and `rust/tests/web/issue-1184-derivation-parity.test.mjs` recomputes with `answerDerivationId` from the browser worker's answer (passing locally; the Rust leg is drafted without a local cargo run). Remaining: the browser worker has no `data/cache/` and so neither persists nor loads (only a node caller injecting `node:fs` does), no JS server route calls `persist` after an answer yet, and the browser worker does not emit the `derivation:` evidence link itself. |

## Issue #1185 Error-Driven Repair Loop

Issue [#1185](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1185) (E149)
asks the executor not to stop at the first failed step: the compiler or
runtime diagnostic in the raw failed output is formalized into structured
data, the error text is searched, a fetched source that addresses the exact
error is retained as a fix, and the failed step is retried on a bounded
ladder — with every attempt recorded as evidence and every dead end reported
honestly instead of guessed around. The audit, the seam survey, and the
worked trace live in `docs/case-studies/issue-1185/`.

| ID | Requirement | Status / Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1185-1 | The raw output of a failed build or run is formalized into a structured diagnostic — file, line, error code, message, and the raw line — through the meta language's shape table, not per-language regexes in Rust. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `formalize_diagnostic` in `rust/src/agentic_coding/repair_loop.rs` runs one generic `{slot}` template matcher over the `language` records in `data/seed/diagnostic-code-shapes.lino` (14 languages), validating each slot by shape so a template cannot read prose as a path or a line number; location lines bind per the language's print order and a python traceback's innermost frame wins; absent slots stay `None`. One captured diagnostic per language formalizes to its exact file, line, code and message in `every_emitted_language_formalizes_through_the_one_shape_table` (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1185_error_repair_loop.rs`) and in the JS root (`rust/tests/web/issue-1185-fourteen-languages.test.mjs`). The E128/#1163 page formalizer stays the deeper route for prose-shaped output. |
| R1185-2 | The diagnostic becomes a search query that names the language and carries the exact error code or message; the fetched pages are read, and a fragment is retained only when it addresses that exact code/message. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `search_query` composes language + error code (or a bounded message head) — pinned exactly by `the_search_query_names_the_language_and_the_exact_code`; `repair_step` plans the search, then the fetch of each unseen source URL (never refetched); `page_addresses` requires the page to carry the exact code or cover more than half the message tokens, and `fix_fragment` retains a fenced block only when its preceding window addresses the diagnostic, else the best addressing sentence. Pinned by `repair_loop_plans_the_diagnostic_search_before_any_final`, `repair_loop_records_the_fix_then_retries_the_failed_command` and `repair_loop_stops_when_no_fetched_source_matches_the_diagnostic`, with JS twins in `rust/tests/web/agentic-write.test.mjs`. |
| R1185-3 | The fix is expressed and applied in the meta language — a Links Notation `repair_edit` record written beside the artifact, never a raw text patch. | Implemented 2026-10-07 (this pull request; Rust verified by CI, no local cargo run): `repair_edit_document` renders the `repair_edit` record (language, file, line, error_code, message, source URL, retained fragment, `rendering meta_language`, `applied false`) and `repair_step` writes it to `<stem>.repair.lino` beside the failing artifact, then re-runs the failed command. The apply half — rendering that record back into the target language and editing the source — was the #1167/E132 renderer's seam and is now delivered: `rust/src/agentic_coding/repair_apply.rs` parses the record (`parse_repair_edit`), splices the retained fragment over the located line re-indented to that line's indentation (`splice_repair_edit`), and accepts the result only when the meta-language CST parses the whole rendered program as valid (`render_repair_edit`); a record with no retained fix, no location, a line out of range, a language the CST engine does not read, or a rendering that does not parse is refused with a named gap and never written. `repair_step` applies it (`RepairOutcome::ApplyFix`, a `write_file` of the rendered source) when the record and the artifact were both written this turn and the record is not older than the artifact, then re-runs the step. JS twin `js/agentic/repair_apply.mjs` and `applyFixPlan` in `js/agentic/repair_loop.mjs`; the JS root has no CST engine, so without a validator handed in it refuses as `unvalidated`. Pinned by `rust/tests/unit/issue_1185_repair_apply.rs` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1185-repair-apply.test.mjs`. |
| R1185-4 | Retries are bounded, and the bound is reported honestly when reached. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `MAX_REPAIR_RUNGS = 3` caps the ladder; the caller owns the rung counter (a retry that fails again re-enters one rung higher), `repair_step` returns `Stop(Exhausted)` at the top, and `ladder_note` renders "rung {rung} of at most {max_rungs}" from the seed template rather than truncating silently. The executor now reports it: `plan_symbolic_command_reroute` (`rust/src/agentic_coding/command_reroute.rs`, twin `js/agentic/command_reroute.mjs`) runs `repair_step` and, on a stop, appends `stop_note` to the failure report, so a spent ladder reaches the answer. Pinned by `stop_note_reports_the_spent_ladder_and_is_silent_without_a_rung` and `rust/tests/web/issue-1185-stop-note.test.mjs`. |
| R1185-5 | Every attempt is recorded as an evidence chain reachable from the answer's derivation. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `attempts_from` reconstructs the chain from the transcript (diagnostic, query, candidate fix, applied, resolved) and `evidence_document` renders it as one `repair_attempts` record with `attempt_count` and one `repair_attempt` row per attempt, in the form #1184's derivation record attaches. The executor attaches it: a stopped loop's `stop_note` follows the honest note with the `repair_attempts` record in a fenced `lino` block in the final answer (Rust and JS roots), pinned by `stop_note_names_the_unresolved_need_and_carries_the_attempt_chain` and its JS twin. |
| R1185-6 | When no fetched source matches, the loop reports an unresolved need; it never fabricates a fix. | Implemented 2026-10-07: `Stop(NoMatch)` is returned when every fetched page was read and none addresses the diagnostic, `plan_repair` yields `None` so the caller falls back to today's honest failure report, and `unresolved_note` names the query and says the need is unresolved rather than guessed. The note is no longer only available: the executor appends it (with the attempt chain) to the failure report whenever the loop stops on `NoMatch`, in the request's language. |
| R1185-7 | The loop is uniform across all fourteen emitted languages. | Implemented 2026-10-07: the shape table carries all fourteen (rust, typescript, javascript, kotlin, scala, java, go, python, c, cpp, csharp, ruby, php, swift); matcher, search, retention, ladder and stops are language-agnostic, and the loop's prose renders through `localized_response`. A fourteen-language table is pinned in both roots (`every_emitted_language_formalizes_through_the_one_shape_table`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1185-fourteen-languages.test.mjs`). Writing it found a PHP defect: the `{file} on line {line}` location row read the whole `PHP Parse error: … in /x.php on line 5` line as a path and dropped the diagnostic; PHP's location now sits inside its patterns (`an_inline_php_location_does_not_swallow_the_diagnostic`). |
| R1185-8 | Three-roots parity: the same loop reachable from the js and ts roots (`formal-ai translate --to js\|ts`). | Implemented 2026-10-07: the JS root `js/agentic/repair_loop.mjs` mirrors every public function of the Rust module and `js/agentic/command_reroute.mjs` drives it as the Rust executor does (`rust/tests/web/agentic-write.test.mjs`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1185-stop-note.test.mjs`, `rust/tests/web/issue-1185-fourteen-languages.test.mjs`). The TS root is `ts/agentic/repair_loop.mts` (with every other `js/agentic` module as `.mts`), rendered by `scripts/translate-es.mjs --write` and gated by its `--check` (`rust/tests/web/translate-es.test.mjs`). Boundary: like `ts/worker`, the TS root is the canonical rendering, not separately executed; the native `formal-ai translate` leg owns only the `.js`→`.ts` set, and `data/parity/cross-runtime-synthesis.json` gains no diagnostic cases. |

Traceability: the shape table is `data/seed/diagnostic-code-shapes.lino` with
its byte-identical embedded mirror `rust/embedded/data/seed/diagnostic-code-shapes.lino`;
the response templates are `data/seed/multilingual-responses-repair.lino` with
its byte-identical mirror `rust/embedded/data/seed/multilingual-responses-repair.lino`;
the loop is `rust/src/agentic_coding/repair_loop.rs`; the probes are
`rust/tests/unit/issue_1185_error_repair_loop.rs` (twelve tests: rustc/kotlinc/
python-traceback formalization, no-shape refusal, search-before-final, no-match
stop, bounded ladder, non-diagnostic decline, record-then-retry, Links Notation
record, attempt-chain evidence, bounded query, planner-contract call shapes).

Wiring the main session owes (the loop is delivered inert by design, like an
unregistered cue table): `pub mod repair_loop;` in
`rust/src/agentic_coding/modules.rs`; `mod issue_1185_error_repair_loop;` in
`rust/tests/unit/mod.rs`; the two seeds registered in
`data/meta/seed-registry.lino` (`diagnostic-code-shapes` bundle,
`multilingual-responses-repair` bundle + `lexicon response`) with the embedded
registry refreshed; and the executor hookup — the failure branch of
`plan_symbolic_command_reroute` in `rust/src/agentic_coding/command_reroute.rs`
consults `repair_loop::plan_repair` before returning `AgenticPlan::Final`,
threading a `repair_rung: u8` through `RecipeProgress`. The exact snippet is
in the module's doc comment and the case study.

## Issue #1186 Formalization as a User-Facing Task

Issue [#1186](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1186) (E150,
part of the E127 umbrella #1183): "Formalize in first-order logic: Every
student who studies passes the exam." answered with the canned web-search
paragraph on 0.347.0. The issue asks for a formalization handler that parses
a quantified sentence into a clause, renders it into first-order logic, Lean
and Rocq, deformalizes it back in en/ru/hi/zh with a structural round trip,
and does so identically in all three roots without memorizing any probe.
R1186-1 through R1186-9 are the issue's R1–R9; R1186-10 is the per-language
probe set its "Probe set and tests" section specifies. The audit and the
